💡 Key Takeaways
  • The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday confirmed Steve Rogers's choice to go back in time to live with Peggy Carter in Avengers: Endgame kickstarts the plot of the upcoming movie.
  • It has been revealed that but, there's one timeline question I can't figure out: what does that mean for Old Steve Rogers?
  • It's a debate Marvel fans are having in the wake of the trailer, and nobody seems to agree.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday confirmed Steve Rogers's choice to go back in time to live with Peggy Carter in Avengers: Endgame kickstarts the plot of the upcoming movie.

It has been revealed that but, there's one timeline question I can't figure out: what does that mean for Old Steve Rogers? At the end of Endgame, Sam Wilson is given the shield by an elderly Steve, who grew old in the past with Peggy. So, if he actually had to return to the present to help fight Doctor Doom, shouldn't the old Steve have already lived through Doomsday?

It's a debate Marvel fans are having in the wake of the trailer, and nobody seems to agree.

Sooooo Do we think this Steve went through the events of Doomsday or?November 22, 2026.

It has been revealed that "I keep going back and forth about this but probably? The only way for Doomsday Steve to have any stakes is if it's the same one, rather than a fresh branch variant created by Doom's disruption," thinks one Marvel fan.

"When Loki comes back and talks to him in the past, he created another timeline. The old Steve Rogers is a different Steve from the Doomsday, although they had the same starting point," says someone else.

"I'd be a little disappointed if he didn't. Seems like there's a fantastic opportunity to make this hit harder upon a rewatch. I personally wouldn't pass up the opportunity. It even goes as far to present that Sam Wilson survives and leads the newly introduced Avengers proudly," thinks another fan.

Sources indicate that "My guess is No. Since Endgame explained that once something happened, it happened, and any change in the past will only create another timeline – meaning this old Steve gave Sam the shield, and only later they met in Doomsday – then this old Steve is but a variant of Doomsday Steve," is another person's theory.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

"Ig yes he went through all the events of Doomsday and Secret Wars yet he remained mute because he knew you can't change the future as it will branch a new timeline so he calmly accepted the truth and relaxed," speculates another person.

That's not the only timeline question, either, since it looks like Steve and Peggy actually live across two different timelines in the Marvel Phase 6 movie – one where they're visited by Loki, and one where the Fantastic Four arrive to talk to them.

We don't have long to find out what's actually going on. Doomsday arrives this December 18, and it pits Earth's Mightiest Heroes against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom.

For more, check out our guide to all the upcoming Marvel movies and TV shows for everything else the MCU has in store.

"More than just war and peace": Total War: Medieval 3's diplomacy system will build on Three Kingdoms' backstabbing, with rulers who aren't just focused on you

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Creative Assembly's Total War: Medieval 3 is going to do a lot more with diplomacy, the developers promise.
  • Specifically, Creative Assembly want to create a sense of factions with autonomous agendas and evolving intentions, while placing more stress on questions of geography.
  • In a blog, game director Pawel Wojs hails Three Kingdoms as "a game defined by its dynamic use of diplomacy, where coalitions, alliances and relationships between characters and factions could fundamentally change the course of a campaign." He continues: "We want to build on those foundations, taking what worked well and exploring how we can push it further for the Medieval world.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Creative Assembly's Total War: Medieval 3 is going to do a lot more with diplomacy, the developers promise. Diplomacy! The soul of any Total War game. They're going to build on the example of Total War: Three Kingdoms, which does allow for some gratifying backroom dealing, in fairness. During my first Thringdoms runthrough, I played Cao Cao, a ruler gifted with the ability to hypnotise people into liking him while hating each other. I spent many idle hours instigating proxy wars. Medieval 3 is apparently going to take all that to "latest heights". It is going to make Han politicking seem as sophisticated as texting "get your filthy hands off my bae" to everybody you know on Valentine's Day.

Specifically, Creative Assembly want to create a sense of factions with autonomous agendas and evolving intentions, while placing more stress on questions of geography.

In a blog, game director Pawel Wojs hails Three Kingdoms as "a game defined by its dynamic use of diplomacy, where coalitions, alliances and relationships between characters and factions could fundamentally change the course of a campaign." He continues: "We want to build on those foundations, taking what worked well and exploring how we can push it further for the Medieval world.".

According to recent reports, as regards "believable agendas", Creative Assemble want the campaign AI to display both a survival instinct and the ability to "pursue its own interests instead of primarily being an antagonist to the player". These agendas will span the game's Politics, Economy, and Families systems, with dynastic considerations affecting behaviour. They want you to be able to read another ruler's intent by tracking back through their past actions. They want weaker factions to sue for peace or seek sensible alliances, rather than "stubbornly being entrenched in a war it is bound to lose". Aww, but I love it when Scotland does that.

Recent findings suggest that the game will aim for a balance of long-term thinking and opportunism, with AI leaders pouncing on short-term prospects even as they keep the whole in mind. And then there are inconvenient "ripple effects": you might get involved with a neighbouring succession crisis because you don't want to deal with the fallout if, you know, That Guy takes the throne.

In a recent development, speaking of borders, Creative Assembly also want would-be treaty-makers to think harder about terrain and transportation. "For example: You finally reach a faraway realm with your diplomat, opening diplomatic relations to a realm far beyond your initial sphere of influence," Wojs goes on. "Relations are positive, but meaningless due to the lack of physical proximity. Once that faraway realm has access to a port, a trade route can finally be established. This leads to an exchange in culture and trade, and may finally allow you to recruit foreign units into your service.".

It has been revealed that I have to say, I do find a lot of this language either broadly familiar from previous Twars, or too general to reveal much. There is, however, a closing in-game anecdote from principal designer Thomas Schut that digs into the detail. Schut gives the example of you sending a diplomat to negotiate a 10 year non-aggression pact greased by recognition of another ruler's royal title, in return for their vassalage. Sending a diplomat allows you to negotiate on the spot, but if you'd rather not spare a diplomat, you can also dispatch sealed letters at the price of not being able to see and respond immediately to the other faction's reaction.

Rulers can make public claims to cities, calling on other rulers to support them. Simply conquering and annexing them will damage your standing in every court. You can also forge claims to cities, if only as insurance against wanting to own them someday. Get enough rulers to back you, and you'll be able to throw around grander pronouncements about what you're divinely entitled to. You are the Emperor of Everything! Coalitions will apparently form and fragment over years, old friends turning on each other as their dark plots come to light.

The joy of Cao Cao puppetry notwithstanding, I don't play Total War for the chance to thrash out cunning pacts with bots. I am here to put my archers behind my spearfolk - and hope the other side's cavalry don't notice the cutthroats I've stationed in the woods. I'm more interested in what I've read about Medieval 3's regional levies system. Still, it does sound like Creative Assembly are serious about giving you things to do besides putting other wannabe kings to the sword.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that sony has been crowing about Grand Theft Auto 6 setting a fresh record for concurrent PlayStation players, which isn't bad for a game that's currently only singleplayer. It isn't just beating the records set by the giants of multiplayer gaming back when they released, though. It's also eating their lunch right now.

In a recent development, alinea Analytics reports that Call of Duty, Fortnite, and EA Sports FC 27 all saw their number of daily active users drop when GTA 6 released. "Call of Duty got it the worst of the three," Alinea's head of market analysis Rhys Elliott wrote, "dropping 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M" according to the manufacturer's estimates.

In a recent development, fortnite only lost 28% of its players, the firm claims based on PlayStation and Xbox data—Alinea's Fortnite figures do not take Switch, mobile, or Epic Games Store players into account—An estimated five million of them choosing to buy groceries and fix the stairs instead of parachuting out of a bus over the weekend. EA Sports FC 27 suffered a similar loss. "FC 27's DAUs dropped by about 27% when GTA 6 launched," according to Elliott, "from 5.9M to 4.3M.".

Industry observers note that but where player numbers for both of those games were trending back up four days after GTA 6's release, Call of Duty has struggled to win its players back, Elliott says: "Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days. It's still down 41% from its baseline.".

During that time Call of Duty had a Thanksgiving-themed event, while FC 27 had a Black Friday discount and in-game "Thunderstruck" promotion, and Fortnite's ongoing Treasure Hunters event is adding a bunch of One Piece stuff. If you're going up against a cultural juggernaut like GTA, I guess crossing over with something as massive as One Piece is the way to do it.

As Elliott concludes, this is only part one of the story. When Rockstar comes back for the second bite of this apple its rivals might have an even harder fight on their hands: "When the online component and PC port of GTA 6 hits (some time next year simultaneously, I'd imagine), then the bounce back will not be so obtainable.".

GTA 6 can run at 60fps on Xbox Series X if you use a glitch, but there's a catch

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (380 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6 runs at 30 frames-per-second across all the consoles it's currently available on, including the more powerful PlayStation 5 Pro.
  • Reddit user Meowwie64 devised a way to essentially unlock GTA 6's frame-rate on Series X.
  • In a detailed post, Meowwie64 shared the steps they used to trigger their glitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6 runs at 30 frames-per-second across all the consoles it's currently available on, including the more powerful PlayStation 5 Pro. The game doesn't offer a 60fps performance mode or an option to unlock the frame-rate, but one industrious player has managed to do it anyway on Xbox.

Reddit user Meowwie64 devised a way to essentially unlock GTA 6's frame-rate on Series X. Their hack relied on the Xbox's rarely-discussed Quick Resume feature, which lets you park multiple games in memory and switch between them without having to re-load each game.

In a detailed post, Meowwie64 shared the steps they used to trigger their glitch. For starters, you're going to need a 120Hz monitor display or TV, as the glitch requires adjusting refresh rates.

First, you need to limit Xbox to display at 60Hz under the console Settings menu. Then, you start GTA 6 (version 01.002.001), wait until the six-star logo appears and then go back to Xbox Settings to change the refresh rate to 120Hz.

Before you return to GTA 6, the final step requires launching another game on your console. This has to be a cold boot, meaning the game shouldn't already be running parked in Quick Resume.

After the second game launches, you now need to use Quick Resume to resume playing GTA 6, which is when you're going to notice the higher frame-rate. The Reddit user stated the game could reach 90-plus FPS at certain moments.

According to recent reports, unfortunately, the user also discovered that game-speed appears to be tied to frame-rate in GTA 6, at least when it comes to certain gameplay animations and when performing certain actions. "I have a stable 90fps and everything works fine but Jason's animations run at 2x speed or more," Meowwie64 wrote. Incidentally, cutscenes do not appear to be affected by this matter, so they run at their normal speed.

As much as a 30fps frame-rate makes GTA 6 feel less smooth and potentially less enjoyable to play compared to 60fps or higher, none of the current-generation consoles are capable of delivering frame-rates beyond that. Tech experts Digital Foundry recently explained why even the PS5 Pro isn't powerful enough to run the game at 60fps or even 40fps.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Capcom confirmed as much in a post running through all of the permutations of the shutdown, which is coming on September 29th 2027 at 8AM PDT.
  • The publishers have already stopped selling Exoprimal's seasonal survival passes, with prepares to pull the game itself and all DLC from sale as of March 30th 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that exoprimal, Capcom's 2023 team shooter pitting exosuited fighters against T-rexes, is the latest game to be handed an expiration date. Its online services will cease as of late September 2027, rendering it unplayable, with the game set to be delisted from stores in March.

Capcom confirmed as much in a post running through all of the permutations of the shutdown, which is coming on September 29th 2027 at 8AM PDT. "We cannot thank you enough for the love and support you have shown over the years, and we sincerely apologize for the gravity of this announcement," they wrote.

The publishers have already stopped selling Exoprimal's seasonal survival passes, with prepares to pull the game itself and all DLC from sale as of March 30th 2027. Those who already own Exoprimal will be able to re-download it in the time between it being pulled from stores and the server shutdown in September, meaning there's plenty of time to hop in for a final few rounds of dino shooting if you fancy.

Recent findings suggest that it's long seemed like only a matter of time before the dino shooter was taken offline, with Capcom having stopped releasing upcoming seasonal additions to it all the way back in July 2024. So, this seems more like a natiral petering out than an instance of an online game being cut down in its prime or not long after launch, as we've seen recently with extreme cases like Highguard. As such, one would hope there's a chance plenty of Exoprimal devs have already been redirected onto other Capcom games, minimising the amount who might be left in the often precarious position of having nothing immediate to work on following this shutdown.

It's fair to say Ed Thorn (RPS in peace) wasn't a fan of Exoprimal on reviewing it at launch. "I thought Exoprimal somehow managed to make dinosaurs versus mechs, aka the coolest concept ever, boring in my review-in-progress,"he wrote. "I held out hope it would improve, though, as lots of commenters assured me it's fun side would finally surface. "Just play several more hours and things really open up! Variety in the dinos, in the modes, in just about everything!". To some extent, they were right. There are fun moments to be had as you queue up for Dino Survival and suddenly, remarkably, things have changed a bit.

"But the game doesn't respect your time. It forces you to sit through hours of repetitive dino-slaying and then only offers you the chance, the chance to slay dinos in a way that isn't excruciatingly samey. Even as someone who finds the fun in mindless carnage, I'd much rather ditch my mech suit and let the dinosaurs run rampant. The dinosaurs don't deserve this.".

That's not exactly as positive a eulogy as the one offered by Capcom, but not all games are destined to stick the landing and be universally beloved mega-hits, especially those wading into the live service maelstrom.

GTA 6 Gives PS5 a Very Rare Win Over Switch 2 in Japan

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At this point, it’s well known that Switch 2 is by far the market leader in Japan.
  • While the PS5 still commands some marketshare, it gets dominated by the Nintendo machine on a weekly basis.
  • GTA 6’s launch is significant, then, because for the first time in a while it’s pushed Sony’s console in front of the Switch 2 – albeit only by a few thousand units.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At this point, it’s well known that Switch 2 is by far the market leader in Japan.

While the PS5 still commands some marketshare, it gets dominated by the Nintendo machine on a weekly basis.

GTA 6’s launch is significant, then, because for the first time in a while it’s pushed Sony’s console in front of the Switch 2 – albeit only by a few thousand units.

According to Famitsu’s latest report, the PS5 sold 41,472 units through the week ending 22nd November, while the Switch 2 managed 36,817 units.

This is an incredibly rare scenario, and likely won’t be repeated again (if ever). But it reveals that with the right software, Sony can put up a fight domestically against Nintendo.

The tech giant’s been taking the region a lot more seriously under Japanese CEO Hideaki Nishino, launching more affordable region locked units to try and stimulate interest.

This week saw the release of the latest Midnight Black model, which certainly helped contribute to the sales.

But PS5’s success was primarily motivated by GTA 6, which sold a very respectable 200,759 units at retail for the week.

That’s slightly less than GTA 5’s 304,752 units opening in 2013, although remember digital buying habits have changed dramatically in the last 13 years, and GTA 6’s physical release was not particularly compelling as it doesn’t include a disc.

A good week for Sony in its home region, then – one that’s unlikely to be replicated, but should be taken as a sign it can compete with the right lineup and pricing model.

[source famitsu.com, via gematsu.com].

  • Deckard serves as more of a supporting character in Villeneuve’s heavily praised film, which reveals the former Blade Runner to be in hiding in the ruins of Las Vegas 30 years after the events of the OG film.
  • In a recent development, since walking out of the theater after seeing the film for the first time in 2017, I’ve wondered about Deckard and Ana’s fates, especially with the looming war between humans and Replicants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that blade Runner 2049, in my humble opinion, is a science-fiction masterpiece. The Denis Villeneuve-directed sequel not only expertly builds upon Ridley Scott’s 1982 film, but it also adds to the mythology in interesting ways. Additionally, the film includes a stellar performance from Harrison Ford, who reprises his role as Rick Deckard. In the near decade since the film’s release, I’ve been wondering about Deckard’s ultimate fate. So, when CinemaBlend spoke to the creator of Blade Runner 2099, I asked for her take.

Deckard serves as more of a supporting character in Villeneuve’s heavily praised film, which reveals the former Blade Runner to be in hiding in the ruins of Las Vegas 30 years after the events of the OG film. Found by Replicant Runner K (Ryan Gosling), Deckard is eventually revealed to have fathered a child with his late replicant partner, Rachel. That child is eventually revealed to be replicant-memory-maker Dr. Ana Stelline (Carla Juri), with whom Deckard reunites at the end of the film, thanks to K.

In a recent development, since walking out of the theater after seeing the film for the first time in 2017, I’ve wondered about Deckard and Ana’s fates, especially with the looming war between humans and Replicants. Blade Runner 2099 creator/showrunner Silka Luisa is also a major fan of the franchise and, when she was asked for her take on what happened to Ana and Deckard, she shared some surprising comments with CB:.

Recent findings suggest that I never asked Michael Green, because I'm sure — he was the screenwriter for 2049, and there's just no world [where] he didn't know what happens. But I almost didn't want to know. What I love about Blade Runner is that so much of it can exist in your own mind, and the world feels so rich that it inspires you to create your own stories within it. And something about that period not being totally defined is exciting, because we can all suggest different things. Yeah, so I don't have a definitive answer.

Considering how major a Blade Runner fan Luisa is, I’m honestly shocked over her not asking Michael Green (who shares 2049 writing credits with Hampton Fancher) for a definitive answer on Deckard and Ana. I can, however, also see Luisa’s point, though, as this franchise does leave certain plot threads open-ended, leading to fan speculation. This answer also tracks with the EP’s approach to 2099, which is a standalone piece that doesn’t have direct references to its big-screen predecessors.

In a recent development, while Blade Runner’s ending remains controversial in some circles, the discussions surrounding 2049’s conclusion arguably aren’t as tense. Villeneuve’s film went through different alterations during development, and even the ending changed. Fancher previously disclosed that the original blueprint was for Deckard to die. While that could’ve been powerful (if crafted effectively), I’m fine with Deckard not biting the significant one, considering it leaves the door open for a direct sequel. And Silka Luisa is down for that as well:.

I really hope they make another. I really hope they make a sequel, just as a fan, to be honest.

For right now, though, fans can return to this dark, futuristic universe by way of 2099. The limited series centers on dying Replicant Blade Runner Olwen (played by Michelle Yeoh) and Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human posing as a Replicant. While fans won’t be getting answers on Deckard, the show covers plenty of ground in other respects. And, who knows, maybe we’ll actually get that 2049 sequel one day.

Industry observers note that all episodes of Blade Runner 2099 will begin streaming for Prime Video subscription holders on November 25 amid the 2026 TV schedule. Blade Runner 2049 can also currently be streamed on Prime, and it’s available to watch for free on Tubi.

Welcome to the dawn of the Internet. Your best friend, elite hacker mega_hurtz, is missing, presumed dead. All signs point to an assassination by the Federal Bureau of Cyber Security and the all-powerful Axis Megasystems. To uncover the truth, you’ll need illegal scripts and righteous hardware to hack your way through the Bureau’s high-security House of Cards network.

Chat with the freaks and geeks of cyberspace’s underbelly, who task you with defeating security systems and snooping through compromised desktops. All to unravel a conspiracy more sinister than you could ever imagine.

In a recent development, no coding skills? No problem! All you need is a deck, a 56kbps modem, and a healthy disregard for authority.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gaming tech giant Nvidia has decided to reinstate Jensen Huang as its president and CEO, despite allegedly saying it wouldn't, and despite a string of extramarital affairs and investigations into alleged bullying, workplace harassment, and humiliation.

It has been revealed that "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers," Nvidia's Chair Harvey C. Jones confirmed on behalf of the Nvidia's board today - the same person reported as saying the board "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

"We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's chief financial officer.".

Sources indicate that in the same press release, Huang said he was "honoured" to return to the organization "at the beginning of a upcoming industrial revolution". "I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment," Huang said.

However, the investigation into one of Huang's extramarital affairs - the one with the person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy - will "proceed to conclusion". The tech giant also stated it formed a "National Security and Export Control Committee", with independent directors, in relation to this.

It has been revealed that huang resigned on 12th November a few days after his affair with the alleged Chinese spy came to light. Two subsequent affairs - both said to be with Nvidia employees and therefore his subordinates - were unearthed not long after, putting increased pressure on Huang and Nvidia.

Since his departure, Nvidia stock has tanked, and as news of his reinstatement spreads around the world, it has sharply recovered again.

So, whether you're doing it for Yasmani or for yourself, here's how to steal a GTA 6 ATM:.

To do any of this, you need a winch. To get a winch, you need to take a suitable GTA 6 car, preferably some form of pick-up truck or large off-roader, to a mod shop. #200640. Inside Retro Reset, the "really inspirational" father and son project teaching kids about classic games hardware from aboard a converted bus

📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

Inside Retro Reset, the "really inspirational" father and son project teaching kids about classic games hardware from aboard a converted bus

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (1960 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • At first the kids jostle to get to the games that they know.
  • Luke’s knowledge is beautiful but the students also find him approachable.
  • The bleeps and blips start from the machines as the students start playing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At first the kids jostle to get to the games that they know. "Welcome to the Retro Reset Bus," says Luke Stoner as the students push to get to the screen that’s caught their eye. Sonic on the Sega Mega Drive is the first they see, and the quickest student to get on board the bus looks triumphant as he nabs the stool in front of the console. Jason, Luke’s dad, asks him what he thinks about the graphics – slightly grainy and slightly pixelated – but he’s not at all bothered and soon engrossed. After a few minutes, though, his eyes keep moving to the back of the bus where "Jackson is a wally" is now emblazoned across a flickering screen in seven different colours. Jackson then gives out a chuffed yell when his code finally works after a couple of restarts. His retort to his mate appears on the 1981 BBC Micro Model B‘s screen as the other students crane to have a look. This is, incidentally, the machine that turned a national broadcaster into a computer retailer (with help from Acorn), says Jason.

Luke’s knowledge is beautiful but the students also find him approachable. As Jason shares: "It’s really inspirational for kids coming onto a bus that they can talk to someone younger like Luke, who knows his stuff and has made something incredible happen." One student asks where Minecraft is and Luke explains that it doesn’t fit the parameter of being more than twenty years old yet, sharing details of when it was published and by who. Roblox could be included, but Luke isn’t keen because of recent controversies around safety. When this group are reluctantly herded off the bus by even more reluctant teachers, another heads in with just a little gap for resetting the machines and cramming a biscuit.

The bleeps and blips start from the machines as the students start playing. One teacher stops at the Atari 2600 and shares that her family has just bought her one. She is loving the daily dose of nostalgia. Luke and Jason move up and down the bus answering questions, resetting machines and showing the students their collection of old phones. One student winces at he is passed the bag that would have carried the battery for a Panasonic EB-3600 "brick" phone from 1989. When Jason says his dad had one, they give that look of pity reserved for anyone over 30 but are also incredulous that anyone would lug that around, especially when the phone could only do calls. When Jason asks if anyone would like to break an iPhone and have a look inside, all of the hands shoot up. He then talks about memory, RAM and chips, brings out a floppy disk; and tells the tale of where the expression "computer bug" came from. Still, it's the game on a tape - Jungle Story for the Commodore 64 - which they all turn away from screens to see. Perhaps we have Stranger Things to thank, but the tape has retro currency and they all think it’s sick.

In a recent development, the event is being run by East Sussex Careers Hub and is specifically aimed at students with SEND (Special Educational Needs and Disabilities). More than twenty-five schools turn up and most teachers leave with a flyer, chatting to colleagues about where the bus could park onsite. Jason says that the response to the bus, since Retro Reset's launch as a registered charity in August 2025, has been phenomenal, and they could easily fill a full week with visits. For now, he is juggling it with work commitments.

The bus was Luke’s idea and inspired by a visit to The Centre for Computing History in Cambridge, where visitors can get their hands on home computers and consoles from decades gone by. The family started thinking about what was possible and finally, after Luke finished college, began kitting out the bus: buying or accepting donations of hardware, researching which monitors would work with the ancient systems, and installing it all within the cabin.

It has been revealed that on a basic level, the charity is telling the story of how technology has iterated. But by allowing visitors to take apart their machines, and giving brief lessons in coding with Basic, it also pulls the veil back on the work that goes into making a game - while opening students' eyes to what they could create themselves. "I guess it’s bridging the gap between the polished and finished latest game," Jason says, "which could be perceived as not achievable for them, to seeing how all that coding came about. Other than making sure they are really accurate with their typing; they realise that coding can be quite simple and something that they can actually do. I would go further and say that when they have written some code, nearly all of them have a big smile on their face." This, he hopes, might be the spark for some students to get into coding, especially for PC games, where under-18s are an underrepresented demographic.

In a recent development, it also hit the road as the popularity of retro gaming continued to surge. According to a Consumer Reports survey published last February, 14% of US gamers regularly play games made before 2000. This is reflected in the staggering stat that the retro gaming market is estimated to be worth $3.8 billion globally, with a projected rise to $8 billion by 2033. Retro-focused videos on YouTube and TikTok rack up millions of views of views, and communities formed on reddit or Discord - some with hundreds of thousands of members - discuss nothing else.

Recent findings suggest that nostalgia is playing a huge part. Atari’s Implicit Conversations is built on just this, creating retro games for modern consoles like PlayStation 5 or the Nintendo Switch. For Luke, though, this misses the point. He likes the click when you put a cartridge in a machine; and he likes that he is just him and the game. The parents of visiting students appreciate this too, and often share how overwhelming it feels to keep their kids safe in the online gaming environment. "Parents of younger children [tell us that] they hate that Minecraft and Roblox can allow their kids to play against perceived strangers. Even the more technical parents say they still miss safety measures and would prefer the games not be online at all," Jason explains.

In a recent development, last month, Ofcom published its Growing Up Gaming summary report, which found that almost two-thirds (64%) of parents of three to 17 year olds who game online are concerned about their child talking to strangers through games or their chat functions. And, while the vast majority of young players go online without incident, it is true that those who use chat functions will likely interact with strangers. The same research found that more than half (55%) of children who game online say they play with people they have never met offline at least sometimes, while one in five (20%) do so all or most of the time they play.

Sources indicate that by contrast, Jason claims that not one student has asked if they can get online, and he’s also never seen one get out their phone when they’re on the bus. Perhaps it is a welcomed break. "We offer a completely safe environment to come and experience these games and machines. That's really what we're here for," he states.

Sources indicate that luke shares too that he became nervous of the data he was sharing with gaming companies, and conscious that this was all being stored, thus making it vulnerable to breaches. He also baulked at what he felt was a constant money grab from gaming companies, including moves that render games unsupported or completely obsolete. Retro gaming is cheap in comparison and therefore more accessible, especially for younger players. "When you tell them that they can get an old console for less than £100 and often games come free when you buy them second hand, their ears really prick up," Jason states. "For a lot of the youngsters, the cost of modern gaming equipment is unattainable. And of course, we explain that they could take old computers and laptops and then load free operating software onto them. This gets them online, often for free. Once they are there, they can game.".

John W. Champeau is founder of Champ Games, a Connecticut-based venture, which develops retro games system primarily for the Atari 2600. He has Scramble, Galagon, Gorf Arcade and Elevator Agent on his line-up. He agrees that price point is a huge part of the appeal of retro gaming. "Atari has released a line of "+" systems that are modern reinterpretations of the class Atari 2600 and 7800 hardware, but at a lower price point but with modern conveniences such as HDMI support, firmware updates, and new controllers," he notes. These systems can also play older cartridges that were released back in the day. "This means that the games themselves can be acquired at a low cost as well, sometimes even free if someone is lucky enough to know someone with a box of old Atari carts in their basement or attic.".

But there may also be something intrinsically different about how these games are designed to be played that is driving their renaissance. In December 2025, Newsweek shared the views of two mental health professionals that "90s Video Games Were Better for Kids’ Brains." In what was sure to be a contentious piece (and perhaps that was the point), mental health counsellor Veronica Lichtenstein, and Melissa Gallagher, a licensed clinical social worker, argued that the very nature of gaming has changed and is now damaging. Retro games had a start and an end – and with the latter came a substantial hit of dopamine for achieving victory. Modern games are designed as "loops for addiction" with no real end; and constant prompts to buy. Satisfaction is constantly deferred. Lichtenstein also says that modern games leave little room for critical thinking, as a quick search online will delivers solutions if a player ever gets stuck.

Recent findings suggest that champeau agrees. "Our games are not designed to be addictive 'time stealers' like some modern video games that encourage players to 'stay online' for hours on end to acquire additional resources needed to complete a game or advance to a new level, etc," he claims, adding: "All of our games are designed to be short burst distractions that don't rely on long gaming sessions to feel a sense of accomplishment.” He says that the lower graphics resolution and primitive sounds are actually a relief for many after years of hyper-realistic gaming. "Retro games distance the gap between game and reality, which was the intention of video games in the first place," he argues.

In a recent development, back on the bus, Sonic may have attracted the initial crowds but it is now Pacman and the Binatone that the students are huddling around. Jason has given up one control for the tennis game to a student and a noisy competition is now taking place. The graphics are basic as is the premise, but scoring is tricky and the battle to get to 15 points hard-fought. The teacher laughs. "The bleeps from that game are bringing back memories," she says as she tries to encourage her students to finish and hand over the controllers. But with faces lit up by the screen and set in concentration, they don’t hear her. This is play for play’s sake, with no distractions, and could be why the games of the past might be just the future these kids need.

GTA 6's best lore drops happen when you're chilling with your partner, so stop leaving them at home all the time

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (719 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, my real relationship be damned, this last week has been all about playing cupid in Grand Theft Auto 6.
  • And, as people tend to do when they're spending a lot of time together, Jason and Lucia talk.
  • Sometimes the interactions are simply fluffy, or funny.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, my real relationship be damned, this last week has been all about playing cupid in Grand Theft Auto 6. I've become utterly invested in keeping Jason and Lucia in love, which means a lot of my time in the game has been spent doing things with my partner in tow. Hitting the gym, inviting them out for a late-night bite, robbing a few jewellery stores. You know, couple things. Things couples do.

And, as people tend to do when they're spending a lot of time together, Jason and Lucia talk. A lot. And you know what? Some of the best nuggets of information about their lives—both their time spent together before the events of the game, and their own individual lives before meeting one another—are tucked away in these interactions that fill the game's quieter moments.

Sometimes the interactions are simply fluffy, or funny. Lucia poking fun at Jason for his deep voice and monosyllabic responses, or them reminiscing about little moments that happened in their relationship before the whole "Lucia ghosting Jason and ending up in jail" thing. Sometimes it's Lucia getting a spam call and giving the bot (and eventual human) on the other end of the phone an absolute earful.

Industry observers note that but then, occasionally, beyond all the comedic conversations and flavour dialogue that give these characters so much life, the game'll drop some proper good lore. I'll do my best not to spoil stuff here, but for almost every complaint I've seen on social media about why certain protagonists did certain things, there's an answer tucked away in these interactions. The kind of things you'd really want to know about these characters? Your best chance of finding it all out is when you bring them together.

I've really enjoyed having lore drops unfold in mundane conversations while walking around, driving, or eating a burger, rather than hamfisted into the main story. They feel like natural breathing moments for the couple to recount the past, or get into the stuff that was happening in the time that they were apart. You know, the exact kind of times actual couples and friends would find the time to dig into these things in real life, too.

That doesn't mean you have to keep them together all the time. Some of their exclusive missions also provide a great bit of insight into their backstories—like Jason's side stuff with ex-army pal Bret Vogel, or the missions that have Lucia in some all-too-real situations with her mother.

I've played plenty of the game flying solo as both protagonists too, and you'll occasionally get some of this nattering just by hanging around in your abode together. But I can't recommend enough that you find plenty of opportunities to bring them together out in the open world. Even if it's just for 15 minutes here and there, you'll uncover a whole lot about who they were before we first got to know them as the player. And as someone who has really enjoyed learning just about everything about these two as I can, it's been one of my favourite parts of the game so far.

It's a bit surprising this crossover hasn't already happened, to be honest, given IO Interactive is the studio behind both of the games, but it's now been confirmed a Hitman and 007 First Light collaboration is happening.

Industry observers note that the content is live from today until 24th December 2026, and it takes the form of a newly introduced Elusive Target in Hitman. Lenny Kravitz, who is playing Bawma from 007 First Light, is the next celebrity to feature in Hitman, but this time, he's on Agent 47's side.

Bawma has been betrayed by three of his associates, and he's called in the bald assassin to take them down.

Up for elimination are Horace Stockton, Oswald Spoon, and Zui.

The newly introduced set of Elusive Targets and the mission hosting them brings with it the likeness and voice of Lenny Kravitz, who you'll hear from throughout the level via Agent 47's earpiece.

"Bawma is such a fun and interesting character to portray, so I was excited to step back into a latest world with him for 007 First Light," said Kravitz. "Seeing Bawma team up with Agent 47 is something I think fans of both games are going to love.".

The mission will be available until 24th December, but if you own a copy of the game, then you'll retain permanent access to the Arcade version of it. It can also be accessed free of charge for those who don't have Hitman 3, as it's being added to the demo of the game.

Alongside the mission, a roadmap detailing the Season of Bawma teases the following content additions: a fresh Escalation, new Arcade and Special Assignment contracts, a new challenge, a batch of Featured Contracts, a new Twitch Drop and an IOI Account reward.

Sources indicate that will you team up with Lenny Kravitz to take down his associates? Let us know in the comments below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar just issued a fresh patch for GTA 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, targeting a few concerns players have been reporting since the game debuted last Thursday (19th November).

The 23rd November patch for the game deploys seven major fixes for the game, including a pretty significant bug that prevented phone calls not triggering at certain points, resulting in a scenario where you could be locked out of progressing the game. The official update is titled 'version 01.002.002', and its weighs in at different sizes on different consoles: it's 603.8 MB on PS5, and 1.6 GB on Xbox Series X/S.

Thanks to an patch on the Rockstar website, you can read all of the updates that arrive with the latest pathc below.

Sources indicate that there have been a few fairly high-profile cases of the autosave not working as the developer intended, leading to a few cases of streamers losing plenty of real-world time thanks to unpredictable auto-save behaviour. JasonTheWeen lost 12 hours of progress on the PS5, for example.

It has been revealed that but there's one issue here the developer hasn't addressed: vignetting. Plenty of players have taken to online communities to complain about the vignette effect that pops into the game - theoretically to help with motion smoothing and various grapihcal elements as the game runs in 30FPS. THe effect is worsened when you're fatigued, hungry, or have some other status effect, but it is present quite a lot of the time, too. Most of the responses to a tweet about the patch posted by the Rockstar Support account reference the vignetting in GTA 6, and the developer has issued no response at the time of writing.

#200636. Latest Update: Any official GTA 6 PC port’s ability to deliver a proper first person mode would be its biggest ace in the hole, so reckon I, a traitor

Latest Update: Any official GTA 6 PC port’s ability to deliver a proper first person mode would be its biggest ace in the hole, so reckon I, a traitor

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1184 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • To be fair, I’ve made no secret of my plans to do just that if you’ve read any of our recent roundups of what everyone’s playing over the weekend.
  • Industry observers note that anyway, I’m writing about playing GTA 6 on console because it’s led me to conclude that a particular aspect of GTA 5’s PC port - one I’ve always rather taken for granted - could be a bigger deal for the inevitable Windows version of 6 than even the usual go-to PC plus points.
  • As Rockstar’s offerings have shuffled away from arcadey rampage facilitators and ever deeper into the mould of uber-detailed life of crime sims, however, they've also began letting players see things directly through the eyes of the crim whose blood-splattered shoes they’ve stepped into.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I’ve been playing GTA 6 on PS5.

To be fair, I’ve made no secret of my plans to do just that if you’ve read any of our recent roundups of what everyone’s playing over the weekend. I can understand why it might leave a sour taste in the mouth, but it is what it is. No corporate gun has been pointed at my head as a mandate to temporarily forsake my PC and play the major game of the moment is forced into my hands.

Industry observers note that anyway, I’m writing about playing GTA 6 on console because it’s led me to conclude that a particular aspect of GTA 5’s PC port - one I’ve always rather taken for granted - could be a bigger deal for the inevitable Windows version of 6 than even the usual go-to PC plus points. You know, better graphics, superior performance, and modding. Historically, Rockstar’s crime sandboxes are games played from the third person perspective. That shot lingering behind Niko Bellic as he jogs around Brooklyn with a rocket launcher or following the damn bike of CJ as he in turn follows that damn train. This is the default way GTA’s breakneck action is presented to the player and was with GTA 5 at launch.

As Rockstar’s offerings have shuffled away from arcadey rampage facilitators and ever deeper into the mould of uber-detailed life of crime sims, however, they've also began letting players see things directly through the eyes of the crim whose blood-splattered shoes they’ve stepped into. In order to do that, while simultaneously pushing the detail and graphical boundaries of their rendered worlds, Rockstar have needed to squeeze every bit of juice they can from the available hardware. Red Dead Redemption 2 managed to include a full first person mode at launch. GTA 6 hasn’t been so lucky, even if there are moments when bringing up your phone or reading a note temporarily lodges the camera into Jason and Lucia’s noggins.

There is a way to glitch yourself into a more permanent first person perspective, but it’s naturally not got the polish that a proper first person mode would. What it does do is make clear that, with vehicle interiors lavishly detailed and some gun animations looking natural rather than janky, any port using the PC's extra horses to deliver a proper first person mode seems a no brainer, if not something already set in stone.

Assuming that is the case, I frankly can’t see why first person won’t become the go-to perspective on PC. Even more so than RDR2, GTA 6 feels like a game built to belong in first person. It dedicates so much time and energy to engaging you in every aspect of Jason and Lucia’s routines, rendering everything from eating to working out to doing up a house (and the acts involved in doing a robbery, I guess) in such exhaustive detail and depth that it’s almost beyond parody.

Notifications ping about you needing to finish a bench pressing session where every rep involves holding and releasing R2 and L2 at just the right time. An app tells you you’re hungry, so you wander over to the fridge, pick out a protein shake to down, then press R2 to lob the bottle in the bin, assuming you’re keen to keep your flat tidy. Shopping trips see you pick up groceries off shelves, stow them in a bag, then run home with it tucked under your arm because you’ve brought a motorbike and forgotten it lacks a boot. Every stickup begins with the ritual of picking your longarm gun out of your car’s boot, where it might have sat next to a bag of drugs you’ve stowed to deliver to a fence later. Stopping off to switch cars and clothes to throw the cops off your scent is no longer just for overenthusiastic roleplayers.

Recent findings suggest that the fact that the game goes to such lengths only to maintain the detachment inherent to the third person view feels bizarrely antithetical at times, like an exhibition of a tiny Fabergé egg that you’re forced to view through a telescope from the surface of Mars. The massive efforts of Rockstar’s developers - many of whom are right now trying to gain formal union recognition or have been fighting the manufacturer at an employment tribunal over firings they argue were unjust - went into putting together an artwork that regularly ends up at an arm’s length out of necessity, despite packing intricacies likely best seen through a magnifying glass.

Sources indicate that enter the PC release. And possibly nothing else offering the same bang for your buck around the same time. With GTA 5, the PS4 and Xbox One got an enhanced version of the game around the time of the PC port, offering a number of extra features - including a first person mode. Rockstar were quick to rule out GTA 6 getting 60 or 40fps performance modes on current console hardware due to a lack of horses, and if that also applies to a first person mode, then such a thing might only come with the next generation of consoles. That’d be the PS6 and Xbox’s Project Helix, neither of which seem hugely imminent and could well end up boasting ludicrous prices thanks to the ongoing memory shortages.

So, those who already own a PC capable of running any GTA 6 port could be in the best position to enjoy the game from a Jason and Lucia-eye view the moment such a thing becomes possible. Sure, it would also look and run better, but to be brutally honest I’ve found it looks damn gorgeous and runs acceptably on PS5. Sure, modding will no doubt spring up must-have additions, but the base game already works in plenty of the roleplaying mechanics and in-depth side-jobbing that a lot of popular GTA 5 mods delivered.

Sources indicate that thus, that window as the place to play GTA 6 as it feels intended, in first person, is what I’d presently peg as the best chance for the crimsim to be not just a great game you can play on PC - as I’d argue Red Dead Redemption 2 and GTA 5 are - but a great PC game that’s inarguably best experienced on our platform of choice. I don’t think writing that is falling into the trap it’s easy to end up in with substantial games that hit console first: declaring in salesman-like fashion that they’ll of course be better on PC by default, in a manner that sometimes feels a bit like you’re trying to convince yourself that you’ve not paid more than a pre-RAM crisis console buyer for nothing.

Industry observers note that I’d never consider playing Cyberpunk 2077 in anything but first person on PC. GTA 6, from what I’ve played thus far, could be the next uber-detailed open world I spend hundreds of hours taking in the sights of, ideally through the eyes of a highly dangerous and highly stylish operator on the prowl for lucrative underworld opportunities.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Inside the NBA’s latest season on ESPN continues, questions continue to swirl around the show in regard to its future. Longtime co-host Ernie Johnson has officially confirmed his aims to leave the show at the end of this season, and colleague Charles Barkley apparently plans to do the same. There’s been a lot of discussion regarding who might replace the beloved sports commentators, and Barkley recently pitched his successor. While it’s a solid pick, I’d admittedly prefer to see another seasoned pundit take over Barkley’s post.

Industry observers note that barkley – also known as “The Round Mound of Rebound” to some – is definitely someone who loves to speak his mind. So it doesn’t surprise me at all that he’d have thoughts on who might be able to take his place on Inside. The former Phoenix Sun was recently quoted as saying he didn’t believe anyone but fellow ex-player Jalen Rose could replace him at the desk. That comment was brought up to Rose when he was interviewed by Front Office Sports (as seen on YouTube) and, when asked about the job, he mentioned this:.

In a recent development, I love Charles and yes, that would be something that I would be interested in. The one thing I learned about this business is everything isn't transactional. If Charles Barkley is going to say into a microphone that you're the person that he feels like should replace him, you can't write a check for that. Even if it never happens. And so, for him to say that, it's priceless. I'm so very gracious.

Recent findings suggest that the notion of Rose taking over for Barkley is actually quite reasonable, considering his resume as a broadcaster. He’s not only served as a fill-in analyst for Inside the NBA for years now, but he’s also taken on hosting duties for ABC/ESPN over the years. I personally enjoy seeing Rose when he appears on Inside, and his relaxed demeanor usually serves as a firm counterbalance to others on the dais like the vivacious Barkley or Shaquille O’Neal. With that noted, there’s another recurring analyst I’d love to see join the show instead.

Sources indicate that inside has welcomed plenty of insightful and entertaining guest hosts over the years, from the cool Vince Carter to the wise-cracking Draymond Green (who has a rivalry with Charles Barkley). Someone who, for me, has always been a welcome presence on the show is Chris Webber, who’s been appearing on the show for years. He obviously has plenty of broadcasting experience, and he’s a wealth of knowledge when it comes to basketball. I’d say the show would be lucky to have him full-time.

It has been revealed that again, though, this isn’t to say that Jalen Rose wouldn’t be able to do the job effectively. There may actually be a reality in which both players end up on the show full time by next season. However, that’s assuming ESPN is looking to bring on two former players and not get another non-ex-player analyst to specifically fill the void that’ll be left by Johnson.

To be honest, it may also behoove me not to get too ahead of myself right now, as the season is still young. Also, while Charles Barkley’s retirement claim is seeming more likely, he hasn’t said much more about it in the wake of Ernie Johnson’s announcement. We’ll just have to wait and see what happens and how the producers choose to proceed should Barkley leave the fold along with Johnson.

As Dawn of War 4's December release date inches ever closer, a upcoming trailer appears to have teased a fan-favourite character's inclusion in the RTS's first post-launch DLC.

Sources indicate that the trailer, which covers the Commander Edition of Dawn of War 4, includes a breakdown of all the extra stuff packed in alongside this version of the game. This includes the digital soundtrack, three-days of early-access to the game, and the story prologue. It'll also include the Aftermath post-launch DLC too, with its dedicated campaign and newly introduced playable faction.

Now, ever since the Aftermath DLC was unveiled, people have speculated it would be chaos-focused. The design of the DLC logo is black with a gold trim, an often-used colour scheme for the faction. However, which sort of Chaos was left up to debate. That is, until this trailer, where the answer is seemingly given away with a cheeky tease.

In a recent development, in its final few seconds, the trailer shows a pair of glowing yellow mechanical eyes peering out from a gloomy background. This was promptly identified as almost-certainly Vashtorr the Arkifane, a relatively new addition to Warhammer 40,000 and a fan-favourite baddie all around.

In a recent development, vashtorr as a character has been getting a lot of love ever since his introduction in 2023. It was then, during the Arks of Omen campaign for the tabletop game, that he played a central part in the narrative event bridging the game's 10th and 11th edition. Since then he was the main antagonist of Boltgun 2, and was central in the 2025 novel Achmagos.

What this means for Dawn of War 4 is that, if he is a commander of Chaos forces, expect a lot of machinery and demon engines on his side. That's kind of his whole deal. Whether that means he's paired with tech-focused Dark Mechanicum as a sort of mirror to the Adeptus Mechanicus faction already in the game, or if he'll come alongside Chaos Space Marines to better reflect the Dark Angels / Blood Ravens remains to be seen. It could also be a mix of both! We'll have to wait and see.

#200632. Breaking: Letter from the Editor(s) #21: That game everyone is and isn't playing, and how we report on AI

📖 Baca

Breaking: Letter from the Editor(s) #21: That game everyone is and isn't playing, and how we report on AI

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1683 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Hello and welcome to an unusually not-Supporter exclusive ed letter, its paywall laying unbuilt so we can exchange some Real Talk with as many RPS readers as possible.
  • Sources indicate that S'been a weird one, hasn't it?
  • The question of how to cover GTA 6 editorially is one we've spent months back-and-forthing over in meetings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hello and welcome to an unusually not-Supporter exclusive ed letter, its paywall laying unbuilt so we can exchange some Real Talk with as many RPS readers as possible.

Sources indicate that S'been a weird one, hasn't it? The biggest game release of a generation, a bonafide cultural event that's touched everything from the highest reaches of government to B&Q adverts, and yet Grand Theft Auto VI's lack of a PC version has kind of given it the feeling of a well-budgeted fireworks display going off outside your bedroom window. For me, anyway.

The question of how to cover GTA 6 editorially is one we've spent months back-and-forthing over in meetings. Even if you consider "It's too big to ignore" a cop-out argument, the likelihood of it eventually coming to PC - based on historical precedent - is practically certain, making it at least partially fair game. At the same time, no, it is not 'a PC game' in its current form, and enthusiastically plastering the front page with coverage of something most of our readers probably can't play – with, say, a launch day liveblog, or a 100-hour-review-that-isn't-a-review-honest – would just be mad.

I'm quite happy with what we ended up with: continued but not excessive coverage of developments around the game, ongoing reporting on Rockstar's labour concerns, and several consecutive days of irreverent posting about the other open-world crime games you can (or shouldn't) play. Why, then, was this restrained approach on the editorial side paired with near-blanket GTA output from our guides team?

The answer to that is the same answer we've been giving to anyone who's asked why RPS previously went as hard as we did on Baldur's Gate 3 or Starfield or Elden Ring: site's gotta eat. It is almost impossible to overstate how important guides are to the survival of a mostly-free games website, or frankly, how much better Ollie, Jeremy, Callum, Dion, and all our guiding 'lancers are at keeping the lights on than the rest of us. An example, which hopefully won't get me in trouble with the higher-ups for sharing 'business intelligence,' is that my piece on Derelikt - one of the most conventionally RPS-y features we ran during GTA 6 launch week - attracted nought point five percent of the eyeballs as Guides Gang's list of GTA strip clubs.

Some sites would look at that and think, well, guess we ought to stop writing about scratchy indie games and focus entirely on megablockbusters. We never have. Our way might create a bit of a parallel reality, where a section of the site does treat GTA 6 like a live PC game, but when those guides effectively fund, support, or otherwise enable the more diverse and offbeat editorial operation, you can't convince me it isn't the best way that's currently feasible.

It has been revealed that somewhere we can do better, however, is how we cover AI - genAI in particular. To start with, I'll temporarily yield the ed letter writing yoke back to Julian, who's on holiday but did send me this for inclusion:.

We've recently seen an ugly blow up in the comments under a series of articles on RPS and I wanted to address it now rather than wait until I'm back at the start of December.

In a recent development, on November 10th, we published an article about House House's use of AI in the development of Significant Walk. The article drew a huge amount of responses in the comments under the piece and also on social media. This is something we are seeing increasingly around anything to do with AI use in game development. There are entrenched camps on both the pro and anti side of this technology and anyone trying to talk between those positions is liable to get attacked. I want to address that but first I want to offer an apology.

The writer of the article took a comment under the piece and shared them on social media, portraying members of the RPS community in a negative light and inviting criticism from their followers. This came from a place of defensiveness – the conversation under the House House piece had become particularly heated and the writer was becoming the target of several abusive messages – but it was unacceptable to disrespect our commenters and readers in this way. I can only apologise for those who were hurt by this, especially those who were trying to be a moderating voice in the comments. Much as it is not acceptable for commenters to aim abuse at a writer (and I have banned the commenters who did this), it is not acceptable for an RPS writer to do this to a commenter.

I have already spoken to the writer and they are fully aware of their mistake and the hurt they have caused and they won't be doing it again. I hope in time those who were hurt by this can feel comfortable returning to RPS. If they would like to talk any more about what happened, please do reach out to me by email (I will be back at work on December 7th, and I can respond to emails then).

Recent findings suggest that now, onto the tenor of conversations about generative AI. I recognise it has become far too aggressive in the comments. It has gotten to the point that it feels as though anyone who doesn't vehemently and explicitly attack the technology is treated as an enemy. I've not got involved in policing this and so by ignoring it I have allowed it to grow. I can only apologise for the hostile environment this has fostered and that our community have had to endure.

I must admit I am unsure how to fix it entirely. But what I am going to try is writing articles that more openly discuss my own views on generative AI. As you may have picked up from some of my pieces this year, I've been talking to developers about their AI use and opening those conversations with examples of my own. A few years ago I was strictly against this technology but I don't find it so simple anymore. Hopefully by being more open in how conflicted I am about this tool, it will allow for more nuance in how we talk about it and that will help in the responses to other articles.

Once again, I am deeply sorry for the hurt we have caused members of the RPS community in recent weeks, I will try my utmost to make sure it doesn't happen again.

I'd add, in response to suggestions I've seen that RPS could enact a side-wide policy or charter on how we discuss AI, that directives like this tend to be non-starters. Fundamental to RPS is the idea that whoever comes and goes, everyone who writes for the site has the freedom to use their own voice, to express their own opinions. This obviously doesn't extend to getting involved in Internet slapfights or personal insults, and as Edwin has noted under a recent AI-tinged story, a consequence is that our output doesn't always follow a consistent editorial stance. Still, I feel that's a price worth paying for maintaining something that, to my eyes, has always made RPS special - if sometimes a little chaotic. And, despite our recent need of the ban button, the vast majority of our readers are smart and mature enough to grasp that different writers might have different views and interpretations.

For example, I don't think I'm as open as Julian to the use of genAI in games development, to be totally honest. Machine learning can and has done cool, unproblematic things for games-related tech and hardware, as well as more 'serious' business like medical imaging. But I'm yet to see anything out of contemporary genAI that outweighs its combined problems with environmental impact, poor output quality, unauthorised scraping of creative and technical works, its applications in producing misleading A/V material, and even the physical safety of impressionable chatbot owners. To say nothing of the fact that Google's embrace of genAI search results presents an existential threat to sites like RPS, regardless of how many guides to finding Skunk Ape (???) we produce.

In a recent development, all that said, I do agree that we - all of us, fans and haters alike - would benefit from chilling out, and trying to navigate the concern with a little more thoughtfulness and a little less dunking. In keeping with the aforementioned editorial freedom, I can see myself writing less about genAI, not more, though on the occasions it does come up, I will try to articulate my opposition to it more deliberately.

Industry observers note that I'm also profoundly disinterested in anointing myself AI Cop, rushing to banish every confessed Claude user to the stockades; I don't have to make excuses for (or give my Advent Calendar votes to) games that adopted genAI, but if it's a matter of choosing targets, there are bigger fish to fry than individual indie games. As far as the comments go, we still only want to police actual bad behaviour, not any particular AI viewpoint, so hopefully we can join each other in this temperature-cooling and remember that "Be excellent to each other" isn't just an Eighties film reference.

Recent findings suggest that to end on a jollier note, thanks to everyone who followed along with the RPS 100, another Not GTA highlight of the past week (and, indeed, 2026). I reckon this was one of the best, most vibrant lists we've done in years, owing in no small parts to the contributions of Sin, Oisin, and Jeremy P. You can vote right now for the RPS 100 Reader Edition, and our insatiable lust for ranking games will also manifest in the imminent 2026 RPS Advent Calendar, for which the reader-run Guessing Game is already open - with free RPS Supporter subscriptions as prizes. Which you might need, as future ed letters will be back as Supporter exclusives. Look, we're not made of nudity explainers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 is a technical marvel, one that's left a veteran game artist with credits on The Last of Us Part 2 Remastered and Star Wars Jedi: Survivor so stunned, he says he "didn't know this was possible.".

Recent findings suggest that del Walker is a lead character artist at Absurd Ventures who previously worked at Naughty Dog and Respawn Entertainment, and he's been giving his overwhelmingly positive thoughts on GTA 6 to Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier (below). Referring specifically to the game's graphics, he notes: "Everything they're doing is what we have been told never to do in every game I've been on.".

In a recent development, for example, Schreier explains that during his conversation with the dev, Walker pointed to the fact that you normally only see a few characters on screen at any point with realistic hair that actually moves strand by strand, with NPCs usually made in a modular way that makes them look generic. This sort of thing comes in an effort to achieve reasonable scope and 60fps, Schreier notes.

Sources indicate that obviously, though, not only did Rockstar opt for a 30fps target on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, but the devs went above and beyond with the detail of their NPCs, with them being individually art directed and given their own personality traits to boot. As Walker puts it, "It's like looking at a skyscraper, but I'm from the 1800s. I didn't know this was possible.".

Sources indicate that he's not the only one impressed, of course. One game designer on The Last of Us Part 2 has called GTA 6 "the Great Pyramids of Game Development," saying that "people will be asking for centuries how it was possible and we will eventually conclude that aliens made it.".

It has been revealed that it's for good reason, of course. Even with such a lengthy development cycle and a clearly immense budget (that Rockstar won't confirm beyond saying it's not $1.5 billion), GTA 6 really is a sight to behold – there's no wonder that other devs are contemplating the sorcery behind it. As Walker so eloquently puts it, "I don't know shit about fuck. Rockstar do, clearly.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After appearing in both God of War Ragnarok and next year's God of War Laufey, Deborah Ann Woll is about to reprise her role as Faye in Amazon Prime Video's upcoming live-action series.

Variety reports that the God of War cast list is now welcoming a second actor pulled straight from Sony Santa Monica's video game series. Deborah Ann Woll first revealed up in the games as Kratos' wife and Atreus' mother during God of War Ragnarok, but she's also about to enter the spotlight proper in God of War Laufey.

Industry observers note that amazon's God of War cast now includes Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy) as god killer Kratos, Callum Vinson (Chucky) as Atreus, Mandy Patinkin as Odin and Ólafur Darri Ólafsson as Thor. Alastair Duncan is also making the game-to-show jump by stepping back into the figurative shoes of chatty head Mimir.

According to recent reports, earlier in the year, the God of War show halted production when former Kratos actor Ryan Hurst suffered an on-set injury. Bautista soon took over the role and production began again in October - all of Hurst's scenes had to be reshot, of course.

Sources indicate that there's no release date yet for the show, but it's said to follow the Norse era of the games which began in 2018's more serious and stern revamp. Amazon ordered a two-season run for the show, which apparently means both seasons will be filmed back-to-back.

Meanwhile, God of War Laufey was recently delayed from February 2027 to May 2027, giving the PS5 exclusive slightly more breathing room away from Fable, Persona 4 Revival and Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis.

Recent findings suggest that "We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential," developer Sony Santa Monica stated at the time. "On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon.".

While the game puts Faye in the leading role as she battles with gods in a multi-mythological afterlife, the studio was quick to note that her journey isn't considered a side game. God of War Laufey will still connect to future games in the series and, yep, Kratos will eventually be back, too.

Sources indicate that "Genuinely, I thought I was going to be much more offended by it, but one, I'm not on social media, so that helps, and two, I don't know, I feel totally unbothered," Woll said of the online trolls who were targeting Laufey after its reveal this summer. "Because I just know it's great. It's okay if it's not your cup of tea, but in no universe is it bad.".

EA Sports FC 27 to resurrect John Motson with help from generative AI, because apparently football games need someone yelling about goals from beyond the grave

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, in today's instance of a sentence I never thought I'd write, English football commentator John Motson has followed in the footsteps of Darth Vader.
  • In a recent development, EA revealed Motson's resurrection for FC 27 to the BBC, with the deceased commentator's voice being made up of combination of old recording sessions and generative AI.
  • Sources indicate that "My dad was the least technological person in the world," Motson's son Fred said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, in today's instance of a sentence I never thought I'd write, English football commentator John Motson has followed in the footsteps of Darth Vader. In the latest instance of a game featuring a dead celebrity's voice reanimated with help from generative AI, EA Sports FC 27 will soon have Motson offering words about passes and shots that clank off the bar despite him having died in 2023.

In a recent development, EA revealed Motson's resurrection for FC 27 to the BBC, with the deceased commentator's voice being made up of combination of old recording sessions and generative AI. The publishers got permission from Motson's widow and son to do this, and told the BBC they'd not have gone ahead if Motson's family - whom EA have paid an undisclosed sum for the rights to use Motson's likeness and recreate his voice - hadn't been on board.

Sources indicate that "My dad was the least technological person in the world," Motson's son Fred said. "Till his dying day, he had a typewriter on his desk. So I don't think he would have quite understood what the AI was doing technologically - but I think, on the other hand, he was always really keen to get involved in these kinds of projects.".

EA senior game design director Mat Prior stated AI has been used for the likes of lines in which Motson talks about modern players who don't feature in the old excerpts of him calling games. You'd think that might've been the point at which EA began to question why it's necessary to resurrect Motson for the purpose of commentating on games featuring a number of players he might never have watched while he was alive, meaning we don't know what unique calls he might have made in response to seeing them strut their stuff. Alas, it seems that wasn't the case.

According to recent reports, "From a gaming standpoint, it's something we've used for many years - like machine learning to help drive animation systems and so on and so forth," Prior added. "It's not there to replace commentators in any way shape or form...there's certainly no future aims to replace anyone with AI." It's worth noting EA already use genAI to replicate the voices of some living commentators with their permission, with the justification given being that it helps cut down on the amount of work required to record hours of a real human saying different player names with different inflections.

Motson served as a commentator on FIFA 96 through 05, but looks to have been absent from the series since that point aside from briefly popping up for a return in FIFA 19. So, aside from that late 2010s one-off, Motson hadn't been part of one of EA's football games for about two decades prior to this AI-enabled resurrection for FC 27. I'd argue that makes it a lot more difficult to make the case for this use of genAI. It's not like the tech's being used to help maintain continuity with a voice that's always been part of the series' furniture, as is the case with Witcher 3 devs CD Projekt Red's modification of Geralt's Polish voice via genAI in the Songs of the Past DLC following actor Jacek Rozenek's stroke. In that case, the actor was also alive to give his direct permission.

Whether families or estates should be able to permit the use of AI cloning on the voices of actors or performers who didn't give written permission for it while they were alive is a matter of much contention. Actor Peter Caulfield, who's been arguing for greater protections against AI voice cloning through a campaign called Save Our Voices Now, argued in the BBC piece that it should only be allowed in cases where living people have signed deals to allow it.

In a recent development, personally, I think games should probably do without genAI-fuelled celebrity ressurections, especially in scenarios where there seems no pressing need to do so. Even Tupac's likeness being used without any AI bollocks in RGG Studio's upcoming historical beat 'em up Stranger Than Heaven feels unsettling. AI Motson will be added to FC 27 as an optional commentator on November 26th.
