📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has managed to get its claws into just about everyone. Honestly, I can't go anywhere without hearing something from the soundtrack or someone talking about how much fun it is to joyride around Leonida. And now it's even infested the sports I watch.

Recent findings suggest that to keep non-Formula One fans up to speed, it was the Las Vegas Grand Prix over the weekend, one of the newer circuits on the calendar. Third place went to Oscar Piastri. In second place was his McLaren teammate and previous world champion for 2025, Lando Norris. And first place went to four-time F1 world champion Max Verstappen, not exactly very surprising given his history with the track. But it is a little more impressive when you take into account that Verstappen has also put 40 hours into GTA 6, much of which would have been before the race.

It has been revealed that "I played a lot in the evening and in the morning in Vegas," he notes in a stream (via IGN), correcting the idea that he actually spent the plane ride home playing GTA 6 instead of spending time doing so around the race. "I mean I can't go out anyways [in the evening and morning], and walk around.".

Recent findings suggest that verstappen did, however, explain that the aspect that GTA 6 has likely affected the most is his ability to play Minecraft, which he had planned to stream later this week: "I'm so bad when I play too many games at the same time. I can't, I just can't.".

Sources indicate that GTA 6 to Minecraft is certainly a jump, but you can't really blame anyone for trying to maximise their time in Leonida right now. I'll also take any chance to spend every free moment playing the game, the only difference being that instead of subsequently competing in an F1 race and winning it, I spend the next day of work acting like a zombie—a poorly functioning one at that. I suppose people are just built differently, or at least that's what I'll tell myself while I'm on my third cup of coffee in three hours.

I am not the Ironclad, nor was meant to be; am an attendant lord, one that will do to bind a necro, Exhaust a scene or two, advise the Regent; no doubt, an easy tool, Defective, glad to be of use, Politic, Silent, and Impervious; full of high synergy, but a bit obtuse; at times, indeed, almost ridiculous— almost, at times, the Fool.

In a recent development, it has been a while since I played Slay the Spire 2. I return to find the forums full of grief concerning a recently introduced sixth character - a minstrel of sorts, dressed in carpets, who shoots arrows out of a harp.

In a recent development, the short version is that the Fool was wildly overpowered when Mega Crit added her to the early access deckbuilder's beta branch, with a base arrow-shooting mechanic that lets her dish out at least 21 damage in her first turn, and a Repeat Shot card that allows for upwards of 80. She ain't so vicious anymore, because they've just released a "mostly Fool-centric" patch that nerfs a couple dozen or so cards.

It has been revealed that it's not all nerfs – they've buffed Cho Chorus, Quietus and Show Off, among others, while reworking Tune, Flourescence and Rapid Shot. There's a fresh Rare card, Optimism, which exhausts all Sadness in your Hand, while drawing a card for every card exhausted.

According to recent reports, some context: Sadness is a special colourless card, earned by way of cards like Mourning Blow. It remains in your hand between turns and can't be played, making it an immediate hindrance, but you can transform it and use it as fuel for certain cards. Just like real sadness! Best of all, you can turn it into Joy, which grants you Energy. Reading about this complex neurophysical alchemy is making me tired. Shall I give the beta build a go? Do I dare to eat a peach? Are you sick of ham-fisted Prufrock references yet?

Read the full patch notes here. The Fool is an interesting creation, eyebrow-raising damage output aside, and I look forward to her addition to the game's main Steam branch. She can play various flavours of music to modify other cards.

According to recent reports, I do like a weird bard, and I broadly approve of the practice of releasing new early access characters with all the sliders pushed to max, waiting for the cacophonous whining to reach a certain pitch, and then jocularly chopping back their stats. I should get back into Slay the Spire 2. I just have to play [redacted] first.

  • Industry observers note that "Become part of the team working on building, growing, and shaping many of these franchises," the listing goes on.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Banjo-Kazooie - the iconic Rare platformer starring an absent-minded bear and the sassy red bird he carries in a backpack - has been on hiatus for years, but a newly introduced Activision job listing has raised hopes for a new game.

In a LinkedIn post advertising a 'Product Manager, Emergent Franchises' role, the publisher wrote that it's "home to iconic gaming franchises including Call of Duty, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro the Dragon, and now… Halo, Age of Empires, Sea of Thieves, and Banjo Kazooie.".

Industry observers note that "Become part of the team working on building, growing, and shaping many of these franchises," the listing goes on. "As a Product Manager, you will serve as the publishing product lead for an upcoming premium console & PC title, driving the product from concept to launch.".

According to recent reports, if you're scratching your brain trying to remember when Activision took control of the beloved platformer, well, it happened during Xbox's last massive internal shakeup. Amid the mass layoffs and studio divestments, Xbox also made some drastic changes to its corporate structure - Halo, World's Edge and Rare were all slotted under Activision's supervision.

Rare's 40-year history includes almost too many notable games to list, but the internal rejig presumably put Activision in control of games like Conker, Viva Pinata and Killer Instinct, alongside the aforementioned pirate hit Sea of Thieves and Banjo-Kazooie.

The job post is by no means confirmation that a fresh Banjo-Kazooie game is in development, but it is the only series named here that can be considered dormant, perhaps hinting that Activision has aims to revive it down the line. Crash Bandicoot 4 and Spyro: A Realm Beyond lay out a pretty good blueprint for its return, I think.

The last properly upcoming game in the series came 18 years ago with the Xbox 360's Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts, a surprisingly good physics-driven vehicle construction sandbox.

Since then, Banjo and Kazooie showed up as a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros Ultimate. More recently, a fan-made PC port and an Evercade Double Pack have kept the series chugging.

In a recent development, composer Grant Kirkhope was slightly more hopeful about the prospect of a Banjo-Threeie back in September. "I do know of like three companies that have actually physically pitched to Microsoft or to Rare about making another Banjo-Kazooie game, and I don't think anyone was successful," he said at the time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that much like a huge dust cloud gradually resolving into an army of skull-painted bikers, Paradox's post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld continues to take shape in the course of developer blog posts.
  • Recent findings suggest that each band has needs, satiation of which makes them feel more motivated and thus, more willing to follow your orders and work for the good of the tribe as a whole.
  • Industry observers note that it appears to make for some alarming diversity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that much like a huge dust cloud gradually resolving into an army of skull-painted bikers, Paradox's post-apocalyptic grand strategy game Afterworld continues to take shape in the course of developer blog posts. The latest Parablog digs into what I think is one of the game's most interesting aspects – you don't control one single unified civ. Instead, you amass a motley tribe by befriending, conquering, or otherwise assimilating a range of individual wasteland bands.

Recent findings suggest that each band has needs, satiation of which makes them feel more motivated and thus, more willing to follow your orders and work for the good of the tribe as a whole. Some of the needs are more generic – for example, shelter, nutrition, hydration, medicine, social standing, and security against threats. Others are bespoke, shaped by Custom - another in-game social metric - and by that band's origins.

Industry observers note that it appears to make for some alarming diversity. For example, you could have a band that are full vegetarian, and excel at foraging - they won't even eat dried insects, the hippies! You could also have a band of cannibals who have a literal Human Flesh consumption gauge. I see nothing in the latest dev diary to forbid you from assimilating both the cannibals and the vegetarians. Let's, er, not seat them next to each other at the next council meeting, unless we're really running low on finger food.

"All needs can scale by band size, level or other game state elements that make sense," the developers write. "Another thing to keep in mind is that different bands will value different needs depending on who they are or recent events. For example a band that’s experienced extreme hunger will get more motivation from nutrition, while a band on the council will expect to get more standing because of where they are in society, not just because of who they are.

In a recent development, "When all of these things come together, you are invited to pick which bands are important for your tribe’s goals," the blog continues. "Those bands are the ones you will pay the most attention to motivate. When you look more closely at what those bands actually want you will find narratively and systemically immersive choices to make. At one point a band may care about food because you are facing a famine, but then rumors of some dustland horror beyond the tribe borders scares everyone into caring more about security and downplaying their previous preoccupation with food.".

The most "work-in-progress" part of Afterworld's band motivation system is managing the potential gulf between an individual band's needs and overall tribe policy. You can, for example, put troops in settlements to make bands feel "dominated", which "increases their motivation, bypassing the needs, and allows you to run parts of your tribe with the stick, while others get the carrot.".

Recent findings suggest that the developers are "still iterating on this side of the system, but the intent is for such tactics to [offer] various degrees of sustainability for your tribe, depending on your set up and who your bands are". If you try to coerce a band, you run the risk of them blowing up in rebellion as and when the stick is removed. "This can result in cool moments like you taking down a bigger threatening tribe who’s keeping their lower classes under control through forced medical sedation, but it all comes apart when you find a way to sabotage or raid the source of the sedatives," the blog explains. Seems very fiendish! There are many points of comparison here with other Paradox games, of course. Before writing this piece, I asked Mark for his take on Afterworld based on many hours desecrating the Catholic Church and/or wine trade in Crusader Kings 3. He observed that the game sounds a bit like playing the unlanded leader of some adventurers in CK3. Myself, I wish I could make some precise references to the Europa Universalis series, but our resident expert Brendy (RPS in peace) left many moons ago to found some appalling indepedendent website or other. So I'm going to swing for the fences and say this feels like a continent-scale game of The Sims, except with groups of irradiated and tattooed, neo-Bronze age pillagers instead of smooth-faced burbanites. For the most informed appraisal of all, here's Julian's chat with Paradox about the game's procedural history generation - it writes you a fresh apocalypse for every playthrough.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toby Fox has given eager fans an enhancement on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.
  • Recent findings suggest that "Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a upcoming blog post.
  • In a recent development, while the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toby Fox has given eager fans an enhancement on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.

Recent findings suggest that "Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a upcoming blog post. "The game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. All the maps, events, and battles exist. (Although there's still one optional event which is dragging out a bit…)".

In a recent development, while the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing. "Much of the game looks complete… but, some crucial scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing.".

Industry observers note that deltarune Chapter 6 was previously described as a slightly shorter episode that should hopefully set up the game's finale quite nicely. Despite being on the smaller side, Fox stated he understandably doesn't want to rush development and "would like it to be as good as possible.".

And since Deltarune's next chapter is almost past the finish line - at least, in some respect - that means certain members of the team have already moved over to Chapter 7.

"Well, we've only just started," Fox continued. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way".

"Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence.".

Recent findings suggest that deltarune's been on a long journey to get here, but, thankfully, the end is finally in sight. Deltarune debuted as a free download all the way back in 2018, a second chapter then dropped in 2021, the next two introduced together four years later, before the arrival of the most recent Chapter 5 this year.

We don't know exactly how long Deltarune's last two chapters might take, but the good news is that it's already been a pretty fantastic game for years. Here's hoping those loose threads don't dangle for much longer.

GTA 6 has notably debuted without a PC release, landing on PlayStation 5 and the Xbox Series X|S only – a debacle that has, of course, led to fans attempting to get the Grand Theft Auto entry running on computers.

Sources indicate that there are various "projects," so to speak, attempting to tackle an unofficial PC port – but one in particular made rounds recently after Rockstar allegedly took its Discord server down and prompted its lead – an anonymous 15-year-old (as per their own words) – to say "goodbye," noting that "managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle-aged men yell and complain to you on Discord." Well, they're back… and so is their project, Leonida. And, according to a new post on Twitter from "NotRexed," the Leonida lead, they'll provide more information on their supposed GTA 6 PC port in the coming days. "Leonida is NOT dead," they write. "I have been doing a lot of work behind the scenes. I'll have some stuff to show all of you soon." They follow up on this with a response stating that Leonida should feature "native Linux support," with "more on that later.".

In a recent development, obviously, it's difficult to verify anything they say, seeing as this is a (very) unofficial port, should it be happening at all. Rockstar itself hasn't actually spoken on the matter publicly. It all stemmed from notorious GTA 6 leaker "Cyberleek," who recently uploaded an executable file and the Xbox build of the game online. Shortly after, fans like NotRexed picked it up and began working toward a PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6.

Recent findings suggest that I'm not so sure what'll happen from here, but I am personally left wondering when Rockstar will announce an official PC release of the game. It's no small launch, after all, smashing records as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and proving "the biggest launch in PlayStation history" (with Sony reporting "more than 39 million unique players" playing on the PS5 alone). Imagine how those numbers could grow….

We have to make the plot line [happen]. I get that — in the first season — they need to establish everyone. Maybe in the second season they can have a little fun and bring Pete back.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought.
  • According to recent reports, "The exe is out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A PC version of Grand Theft Auto 6 - one from unofficial sources, at least - may be closer than we thought. After suddenly returning last week with a near-full build of the Xbox version, notorious leaker CyberLeek has now posted the missing piece they intentionally held back: the game's executable (.exe) file.

According to recent reports, "The exe is out. Always free. An early Christmas gift from CL," CyberLeek reportedly wrote, as relayed on Reddit. "The torch passes to the open source re-comp and emulation projects.".

Hours later, the recompilation modders and hackers part of the Project Leonida Discord server - the current hub for all GTA 6 recompilation efforts - posted footage of the game booting up on PC.

In a recent development, in just a matter of hours, modders - with the help of Claude AI - managed to turn the leaked Xbox build into a PC port, of sorts. In this Reddit video, you can see the game boot up to the initial setup before hitting a black screen. The build is clearly not yet playable, though Eurogamer has not directly verified those claims.

Shayder, one of the lead developers on Project Leonida, stated in a since-deleted post on X that we should "expect a lot of static recompilation work to be done soon." On the project's Discord server, they later clarified that it could take about a week for the build to reach a playable state on PC.

In a recent development, as for CyberLeek, the leaker is still soliciting donations for a secret project "for the gamers", adding in the build's readme file, "Nobody has to give anything, and every release stays free either way. But every donation is a vote for more of this, and so is every trade of the token.".

Rockstar has not confirmed a PC version of GTA 6, but the company has historically released its games on PC several months after their console debut. In October, a report noted GTA 6's PC version would arrive in the first quarter of 2027, an unusually short gap between the console and PC releases.

In a recent development, these latest recompilation efforts, however, may force Rockstar to speed up development of the PC version. Though the recompiled build may never reach the level of quality or stability of an official port, many of those eager to play the game on PC likely wouldn't care.

#200617. Company of Heroes 3: Operation Torch review - moments of barely held-together chaos squandered by mechanical scripting

Company of Heroes 3: Operation Torch review - moments of barely held-together chaos squandered by mechanical scripting

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1021 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, after waiting three years for Relic to expand Company of Heroes 3's singleplayer, watching DLC after DLC focused on expanding the roster of units available in multiplayer matches, Operation Torch looks like a welcome addition.
  • It has been revealed that having played through the whole thing, I really want to say it's been worth the wait.
  • About halfway through the campaign, I'm put in charge of managing a retreat under a German advance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, after waiting three years for Relic to expand Company of Heroes 3's singleplayer, watching DLC after DLC focused on expanding the roster of units available in multiplayer matches, Operation Torch looks like a welcome addition. It's a new 15-mission campaign set in North Africa. following two US officers as they try to break the German Afrika Korps' hold on the region.

It has been revealed that having played through the whole thing, I really want to say it's been worth the wait. Unfortunately, it's not so straightforward as that.

About halfway through the campaign, I'm put in charge of managing a retreat under a German advance. While I must use my limited forces to hold back enemy troops at the head of the map, I'm also to drive a supply truck to different structures on the map so its crew can evacuate the buildings. It's a fraught start to the mission, forcing me to balance my attentions on the embattled front while also keeping a watchful eye on the vulnerable supply truck. German forces are seeping past the line and it would only take one well-placed anti-tank gun to spell an end to the evacuation.

In a recent development, the tension that comes in those moments, where I'm hopping about the battlefield barely holding things together, is Firm of Heroes at its best. Operation Torch has several moments that reach that height of trying to command chaos, but they're squandered just as promptly as they come.

Industry observers note that when the three structures are broken down, I'm ordered to pull back to a hill outside of town. The mission isn't over, though: German officers are sifting through the abandoned buildings, looking for intel that was missed in the evacuation, and I'm to take two squads of snipers into enemy territory to kill them before they find anything. While it sounds exciting on paper, the mechanics of the mission's scripting make the reality underwhelming. My weakened army is sitting on a hill outside of town but no Germans come their way. In town, German units either stand still or travel in small looping patrols. Navigating the camouflaged sniper squads between them is easy work, but slow going. And even when they come out of stealth to shoot the officers and are spotted by a unit of German soldiers, they walk away from the fight and the Germans don't give chase. This may all be because I'm playing on standard difficulty, but the AI is oddly passive throughout Operation Torch.

Recent findings suggest that across multiple missions, I repeatedly used the same cheesing tactic. I would send a unit with the stealth passive to hide invisibly behind cover near the enemy, with strict orders not to open fire. With my infiltrator acting as a forward spotter, I'd then pummel the enemy with mortars from a safe distance. This tactic worked again and again. I knew, really, that it was no fun to do – turning every battle into a slow grinding down of the enemy – but it was also too effective to ignore when the enemy would never fight back.

It has been revealed that it's a shame so many of Operation Torch's missions hit a bum, overly-scripted note because I really enjoyed their unfurling narrative. Admittedly, my military history is poor, and all my knowledge of the North Africa campaign is drawn from the bits in SAS Rogue Heroes before they go to Europe, but my general understanding is that it was a campaign that saw rapid advances turn into just-as-quick retreats. This plays into Operation Torch's missions where success often isn't pushing the front forwards, but holding the line while covering routed allied forces, or defending a pass long enough for air support to arrive and cause enough damage to force the Germans to slow down. And, because you're battling backwards and forwards over the same territory, Relic employ one of my favourite RTS tricks: throwing you back into the same map but from a different perspective. In one mission you may be on the assault, prizing free the Afrika Korps' grip on a town street by street, but then a few missions later you find yourself defending the same territory from a retaliatory attack. It's unfortunate that the same push and pull isn't as evident on the battlefield.

According to recent reports, relic are experimenters, often reinventing a game's systems between entries in a series or trying out a new mechanic in their expansions. In Operation Torch, the new toy is a choice of unlocks at the end of each mission. After a tank-focused assignment, for instance, you're offered a choice between a passive perk that makes Shermans 25% harder to hit while moving, or another which unlocks a different Sherman variant in your motor pool. Complete the map's optional objective and you also get to choose between a 10% reduction in tank costs and an upgrade that sees all your tanks produced at level 3 veterancy. These perks then apply throughout your campaign. By the final mission, the right side of your screen is a fat stack of passive and active perks. It's a neat idea but, in practice, it didn't seem to make a dramatic difference to how I played. I do like the idea of gradually developing your forces capabilities over a campaign but perhaps the difference needs to be more dramatic. Making your tanks slightly cheaper or harder to hit doesn't make that much of a tangible difference when you're right in there amidst the tracks and trenches.

In a recent development, thus, it really does fall back to the strength of Operation Torch's missions, which are sometimes great but too often a case of rolling over the enemy very, very slowly. Perhaps this is a game best played with the difficulty whacked up high.

While I was hoping for more from Operation Torch, mind, I do hope it's not the last time we see Relic flesh out Manufacturer of Heroes 3's singleplayer. There's still plenty of scope there, and plenty of room for further experiments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stealing an ATM in GTA 6 requires a few different things: a winched vehicle to haul it out of the wall and drive off, plus the dye pack jammer that stops marked bills from exploding pink all over your lovely cash.

There are two ways to get a winched truck. The video above highlights a location at the crop duster landing strip in Frogswater where you can steal one, but you can also mod any truck at a mod shop to add a winch.

If you don't have a truck to mod, there's a unique one you can steal from the Kolt & Associates June Warehouse robbery in Port Gellhorn, just south of Sarena's Bargain Store, which you could then register with Moses and mod at Wasteland Off-Road in the north of the town. You can also get a winched truck around the back of Yasmani's vape shop in Little Cuba—the fence who gives you the ATM tip offs.

You'll also need the dye pack jammer, which you get in the Chapter 3 main mission, Credit Check, for Raul. Once you have both of these, you're ready to rob an ATM. If you complete all three of Yasmani's jewelry thefts (also in Chapter 3), he'll call a little later and offer tips about full ATMs, giving you three for free that you have a 24 hour window to hit. Here's how to steal them.

For Yasmani's tipped-off ATMs I got about 11k-ish per time, so not terrible, but likely not the best way to make money unless you get really efficient at it and invest in a proper getaway winch truck.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A newly introduced report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.
  • "Sources close to Microsoft's looks tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," notes the Windows Central report.
  • The revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: new management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A newly introduced report from Windows Central details how Xbox was reportedly looking into removing the paywall that prevents players without Xbox Live from playing online games, only to potentially renege on its decision sometime during production of the next-gen device.

"Sources close to Microsoft's looks tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer," notes the Windows Central report. It goes on to note that this Xbox Live-free strategy was iterated upon under Xbox's previous leadership, but with Asha Sharma's appointment as Xbox head in February, all that apparently changed. I guess she did promise "radically different business models", after all.

The revised plan has reportedly been altered thanks to a myriad of factors affecting the Xbox business: new management, rising component costs, and a shifting hardware strategy, are all outlined specifically in the report. We've previously heard that Xbox's next-gen console could cost up to $1,800, with a handheld version coming in 2027 and a full release by holiday 2028 (a Helix console at $1,200 would mean a 50 percent increase on top of Series X's current price, for what it's worth). Sharma has stressed Helix will launch as "a family of devices" that will act as a bridge between PC and Xbox capable of playing games from both platforms.

Industry observers note that if Xbox has, indeed, decided to scrap the idea of free online multiplayer access, it'll be a blow to the idealistic 'PC and Xbox' platform that Microsoft has been touting for the past few years: PC players do not need a subscription in order to access online modes, so - right out the gate - there will be a division between one group of players and the other. Perhaps this is why we've heard a little change in the tone of how Sharma and other Xbox bosses are talking about Helix more recently - these hints that the console will be a true PC-and-console hybrid have died down, and been replaced by insinuations that we'll see more of a traditional console with the "ability to play your PC games.".

Xbox has been running Xbox Live as a service since 2002, when it introduced on the original Xbox console. By 2005, it was split into gold and silver tiers to distinguish free players from those that paid. In 2023, the service was fully renamed Xbox Game Pass Core, looping in access to the base roster of Game Pass games with online play.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite a falling-out with the company that led to the creation of the PlayStation, former Sony Computer Entertainment CEO Ken Kutaragi says he loves Nintendo.

For those unaware, Sony's first foray into the games industry was in collaboration with Nintendo, which was looking to create a CD-based add-on for the Super Nintendo Entertainment System (SNES) in the vein of the Sega CD. Sony and Nintendo's collaboration was dubbed the Play Station, but one day after Sony unveiled the collaboration, Nintendo announced a partnership with Philips to create a SNES CD. This led Sony to pursue its own console, with Kutaragi at the helm, resulting in the PlayStation, which sold over three times as many consoles as the N64.

Sources indicate that but despite the fallout, Kutaragi tells The Game Business, "I love Nintendo," adding, "I [contacted them] every week. One of my counterparts there was my best business friend. I love Nintendo games." He acknowledges the idea that PlayStation was made to get revenge on Nintendo, saying, "Many of the media said, 'Sony suffered a betrayal, they will take some revenge.' No. Totally no. We are all friends".

Industry observers note that kutaragi recalls just how much he worked with Nintendo – starting with a proposed disk for the NES, before working on the sound chip for the SNES itself – "I approached the Nintendo headquarters every week by using the bullet train. So, I seemed to be an acting member in Nintendo. [One woman there] assumed I was their employee. I had a very close relationship [with Nintendo].".

Ultimately, it probably worked out the best for everyone the way it did. Sony ended up making the most successful console ever with the PS2, and every one of its home consoles, barring the PS3, sold over 100 million units. Nintendo got a bit of a reality check when the N64 and GameCube didn't come close to Sony, and pivoted to unique hardware like the Wii and Switch. Shame about Sega though….

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia may have finally released a proper cure for their last graphics driver, 621.24, reportedly writing unneccesarily vast amounts of data to some users' SSDs.
  • Alongside delivering enhancements specifically aimed at Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4, Where Winds Meet, and Assetto Corsa Rally, 621.40 lists dealing with the fact "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background" as one of its key aims.
  • Recent findings suggest that as to whether or not it's achieved that, some folks on Reddit and the Nvidia forum look to be making yes-shaped noises, but I'd not quite classify what I've seen so far as 100% proof.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia may have finally released a proper cure for their last graphics driver, 621.24, reportedly writing unneccesarily vast amounts of data to some users' SSDs. A hotfix late last week seemed to have made things better, but not fixed everything. Here's hoping driver 621.40 has managed to totally rectify things.

Alongside delivering enhancements specifically aimed at Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4, Where Winds Meet, and Assetto Corsa Rally, 621.40 lists dealing with the fact "excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg may occur in background" as one of its key aims.

Recent findings suggest that as to whether or not it's achieved that, some folks on Reddit and the Nvidia forum look to be making yes-shaped noises, but I'd not quite classify what I've seen so far as 100% proof. If you've reverted to the last driver which looked glitch free, 621.01, waiting a few more days and seeing if a more definitive consensus emerges might be the best option.

In a recent development, after all, the hotfix which preceded 621.40 also declared war against those excessive writes to file nvlog.nvlgstg, and it ended up stopping the excessive writing from starting right after you boot up and reducing the amount that's written, but not totally getting rid of the problem if an affected PC was left running for extended periods. At the very least, the fact the attempts at fixing the concern have now made their way into Nvidia's main branch is a key step towards the latest driver to hit the company's site and app eventually being excessive write-free.

As we've noted in our previous coverage of the issue, which doesn't seem to be affecting all machines, if you want to check if you're suffering from the excessive writing you'll need to open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do some maths to work out if it's writing little scraps of MB or big bits of GB.

For those of you out there in love with Grand Theft Auto 6's soundtrack, you'll be happy to know that Rockstar Games have revealed an additional 23 tracks as part of the game's deluxe edition album.

These tracks, available via streaming services, include songs from artists like HEALTH, Denzel Curry, Playboi Carti, and more. You can find the full track list on the official Rockstar Games music website.

Some of these artists played a significant role in the game. Justice, for example, helped compose the game's original soundtrack and several of their tracks appear throughout the game. There are others, too.

Both Sexyy Red and Denzel Curry voice characters in the game's later chapters. Others like Kodack Black and Freddie Gibbs also show up, too - that's not to mention the huge number of musicians who make an appearance in the game's many radio stations. Musical talent also played an additional role in creating the TV advertisements and indicates you can watch in the game. Zack Fox is one example, as is Weird Al Yankovic. Both wrote parts of the game's enticing and absurd substantial screen entertainment - which makes sense given the pair's shared comedy background.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Black Friday sales officially start Friday, November 28, and run through Cyber Monday, November 30, 2026, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before it's over.

It's Cyber Monday, and Lifehacker is sharing the best sales based on product reviews and comparisons before the sales are over.

Sales are accurate at the time of publication, but prices and inventory are always subject to change.

Not every Black Friday or Cyber Monday deal is as sweet as it seems. With electronics and tech in particular, you could be buying last year's model that has actually been on sale since the summer—and was maybe a better price a few months ago. Here’s how to avoid impulse buying a misleading Black Friday “deal” and make sure you’re getting the best bang for your buck.

When you see products like food, clothes, or home goods with a substantial "Black Friday" or "Cyber Monday" tag slapped on them, it's probably safe to take advantage of that deal. Chances are it's the same exact product you'd find on other days of the year. The same can’t be noted for a TV, laptop, and other tech deals, where the product itself is constantly being upgraded.

Because tech is always evolving, and retailers want to move inventory before upcoming models come out, electronics are especially susceptible to a practice known as "price anchoring." That's when retailers mark up prices in the weeks leading up to Black Friday, before "slashing" those prices back down, giving the appearance of a deal that isn't really a deal at all. Still, when you see that marked-up number, aka the "price anchor," you might get tricked into thinking you're saving money when you're not. There's also the false sense of urgency that gets created. It's second nature to assume that anything labeled "deal" won’t last long—even when this so-called deal price has actually been going on since the summer.

Price anchoring isn't even unique to Black Friday. The nonprofit Consumers’ Checkbook tracked prices at 25 major retailers over 33 weeks in 2022 and found that more than half the items tracked were offered at false discounts every week or almost every week. Less common, but also worth noting, is a known practice of "derivative" or retailer-exclusive models produced specifically for the holiday shopping season. These versions often feature cheaper components, fewer features, or lower specifications than their regular counterparts. A 55-inch TV from a reputable brand might look identical to the year-round model, but it could have a lower refresh rate, inferior panel technology, or fewer HDMI ports.

Industry observers note that in the same vein, that "amazing deal" on a laptop might come with last year's processor, or a smartphone that's about to be replaced. The problem isn't that the tech is an older model, but again, it's that it probably has been at this low a price, or lower, since the summer. Alternatively, some deeply discounted electronics are refurbished units or open-box returns that have been repackaged. Again, while this isn't necessarily a bad thing, impulse buyers may not fully realize what they're buying.

It has been revealed that the key phrasing here is impulse buying. Events like Black Friday are psychologically engineered to trigger impulse purchases. Limited-time offers, countdown clocks, and "while supplies last" warnings create artificial urgency. When you're caught up in the moment, it's easy to convince yourself you need a new tablet, smartwatch, or gaming console, even if you hadn't considered buying one before.

Recent findings suggest that to avoid a low-key scam, do your research. The easiest way to tell that you’re getting the correct product is by checking the model or serial number. And with online shopping, finding and double-checking those numbers is quick and easy. In addition, don't just compare prices—compare specs. Look at processor speeds, RAM, storage capacity, screen resolution, refresh rates, and connectivity options. A $300 laptop isn't a deal if a slightly more expensive model offers significantly better performance that will last longer.

If you do see a deal that catches your eye, it could pay to wait. Cyber Monday, post-Christmas sales, and even January clearances often feature electronics deals that rival or beat Black Friday prices, all without the famous chaos and pressure. Then again, you risk more “out-of-stock” results if you wait, so the risk is up to you, depending on the popularity of the item you’re eyeing (and how badly you want it).

The bottom line: Don’t fall victim to a falsely advertised lower-quality product, and do a little research to find actually good deals ahead of time.

In a recent development, yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

It has been revealed that nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, November 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

Industry observers note that yes. Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and Home Depot will all have in-store deals, some of which you might not find online, so if you're able to take a trip to your local retailer, keep your eyes open for different deals.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Black Friday sales officially begin Friday, November 27, 2026, and run throughout “Cyber Week,” the five-day period that runs from Thanksgiving through Cyber Monday,  November 30, 2026. But Black Friday and Cyber Monday dates have expanded as retailers compete for customers. You can get the same Black Friday sales early, and we expect sales to wind down by December 2, 2026.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • I say this with some pride – tempered against the fact that this has been obviously an enormously long development, so clearly not everything has gone well – but I would say that our original vision of what Fable needs to be has remained unchanged," Ralph Fulton, one of Playground's co-founders, told our suit-wearing siblings at GIBiz.
  • Recent findings suggest that "There are many reasons that this game development has been long," he added.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the Fable reboot is finally set to kick the release chicken (I'm not sure that's an established phrase anywhere in the world, but roll with it) early next year, following a not small amount of time in development and multiple delays. Despite that long time in the oven having made it necessary to look beyond just the series' classic entries for RPG inspiration, Playground Games' Fable general manager has said the team's "original vision" of what a Fable game needs to be hasn't changed.

I say this with some pride – tempered against the fact that this has been obviously an enormously long development, so clearly not everything has gone well – but I would say that our original vision of what Fable needs to be has remained unchanged," Ralph Fulton, one of Playground's co-founders, told our suit-wearing siblings at GIBiz.

Recent findings suggest that "There are many reasons that this game development has been long," he added. "It's a fresh team, it's a new genre, a new franchise, new technology – although we're building in an engine that we know well. It's also because a Fable game must have a great story with memorable characters and high-stakes drama, and also it needs to be funny and to have that British wit infused throughout it. Then there's combat, the quest structure, and the world of Albion and its people, and the simulations that underpin it. You'd be nuts to take on all of that in the first project, and yet here we are.".

Fulton went on to note that despite that, Playground have worked to ensure their game's scope hasn't grown ever wider as they've made it. One call made early on with the social and economic simming that goes with the likes of landlording and being a dick to entire villages was that the studio "would only model first and second degree ripple effects", due to feeling that "players would only notice or we could only communicate the consequences up to the second degree". That makes sense, not every game can or should be a strategy game like Civ, wherein seeing your actions cause or influence a thousand different tidal waves over time is part of the central appeal. Not every game also has the budget of a GTA 6, which works deep simulation mechanics into a crime adventure, but feels like an exception to the rules even compared to Xbox-backed games like Fable.

It has been revealed that on the other hand, Fulton did make clear that Playground have looked beyond the original entries in the series for RPG inspiration, fearing their game might be left behind if not. "Principally, technology has advanced," he remarked when asked what's changed while the game's been in the works. "In 2015, The Witcher 3 redefined what an open-world action RPG looks like and became the gold standard. And after that bar was raised, the Assassin's Creed franchise changed into this more modern iteration with Origins, Odyssey, and Valhalla, and became like a quasi-RPG.

"All of these games continue to reset player expectations, which means I think looking only to the original Fable trilogy for inspiration would leave us lacking in terms of what the modern audience, the modern marketplace, expects.".

In a recent development, we've already seen some of the ways in which the reboot diverges from its older forebears. As far as I'm concerned, albeit as someone with only a brief dalliance in the classic Fables, such tweaks could go either way. It is interesting to see Assassin's Creed mentioned alongside The Witcher 3 as having changed the RPG game. A game like Baldur's Gate 3 or even Starfield would strike me as a more obvious candidate to point to, so the AC mention might offer some indiction of the direction Playground have taken with their design.

In a recent development, fable is, of course, being backed by Microsoft. The organization are subject to an ongoing boycott by the BDS movement and have inflicted significant layoffs on their Xbox studios this year. As for whether the latter upheaval has affected Playground or Xbox's backing of Fable, Fulton offered a rather nothing answer here about Forza Horizon being good for the studio and the importance of keeping everyone internally in the loop as to how work on the game's going.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sony's revealed staggering statistics relating to the popularity of Grand Theft Auto on PlayStation 5, not least that more than 39 million unique people have played the game there. That's more than the official GTA 6 day-one sales tally of 32.5m copies across all platforms.

Sources indicate that unsurprisingly, with such massive numbers, GTA 6 is a record-breaker on PlayStation. According to the PlayStation Blog, the game has recorded the highest number of concurrent players on PlayStation ever, surpassing any previous record across all kinds of game - multiplayer, free-to-play and single-player.

In addition, PlayStation also saw "the largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day" since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays, suggesting that Rockstar's latest game, more than any other PS5 game released so far, has driven hardware sales. GTA 6 is apparently the first game played on 70 percent of new PS5 consoles.

The average GTA 6 playtime, per person, is a considerable 17.4 hours, the blog states, and the total number of hours spent playing the game is 683 million - a number so high I can't contextualise it.

Industry observers note that microsoft hasn't announced equivalent data for Xbox but I assume the game is a record-breaker there, too, given that it broke pre-order Xbox Store records in the same way GTA 6 did on PlayStation. However, GTA 6 is estimated to have sold far more copies on PlayStation - as many as 75 percent of its total sales, according to Alinea Analytics analyst Rhys Elliott.

Elliott estimated that GTA 6 amassed a colossal 44.9m sales by the end of its opening weekend, and that 33.7m of those were on PlayStation 5 (which still doesn't reach the '39 million unique players' stat Sony has just trotted out) and 11.2m were on Xbox. That amount of sales would earn Rockstar something like $4bn in revenue.

The arrival of GTA 6 has, then, been seismic. The game has wowed critics and dominated conversation not only in the games industry but also across entertainment news and mainstream news. Meanwhile, however, we await the verdict in the Rockstar Games employment tribunal in Scotland, relating to the sudden firing of 34 employees a year ago. Was Rockstar union-busting, as alleged? It'll be a historic ruling if deemed so.

In a recent development, you can cancel your Prime subscription via web browser by first logging into your Amazon account. Amazon has a Cancel Your Prime Membership button on its support page to launch the process, or you can follow the steps detailed on Amazon's page:.

Head to Amazon.com in your web browser.

Hover over the Accounts & Lists menu on the top-right of the window, then select the Prime Membership option.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

Note that Amazon requires a bunch of clicks to finalize your cancellation, giving you lots of “opportunities” to change your mind.

Open the Amazon Shopping app on your mobile device.

Click the three horizontal lines on the bottom right.

Under Shop by Category, select Prime.

On the top bar, slide all the way to the end and select Help.

Then tap the End Your Amazon Prime Membership button and finally click the Cancel Your Prime Membership orange button.

Follow the on-screen instructions to cancel your Prime subscription.

In a recent development, as mentioned, closing your account will immediately end your access. Amazon also offers you the option to pause your benefits and billing temporarily instead of canceling them completely. Either way, your Amazon account is still active—you simply won’t have Prime benefits.

In a recent development, finally, if you have other subscriptions connected to your Prime account, those will end when your billing is up. And if you signed up for Prime through the Android mobile shopping app or the Prime Video Android app, you’ll have to go through Google Subscription to manage your membership.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 has been out for a little while now, and already players are showing off their skills when it comes to the game's many heists. Despite the challenges in getting away clean, some are proving it's possible.

Industry observers note that for one, sneaking into a bank while the vault is open and stuffing your bags full of marked bills is a tricky process of gradually making your way through rooms and taking out guards as quietly as possible. While the police in the clip below were called to an eventual breakout of violence, a lengthy getaway allowed for a cheeky payday of almost $100,000 in cash.

This crew really cracked a whole bank vault and walked out with almost $100K in GTA 6 💰🏦🚔😮‍💨 #gtavi #gta pic.twitter.com/pJyFXREBvY.

One especially impressive element of Grand Theft Auto 6 is how many of its little mechanics interact with each other. As you can see below, if you bring a vehicle with a winch to a cash machine, you can actually pull it off the wall and drag it away from the scene of the crime.

Why rob a bank in GTA 6 when you can just take the whole ATM💸 How to do it❓- Hook the ATM up to a vehicle with a winch- Drag it through the streets until the cash cases fall out- Shoot them open and get out fast, the cops come quickly!(via u/MelloYello917) pic.twitter.com/5eXbULJWP3.

In a recent development, as you progress through Grand Theft Auto 6, the game actually introduces you to both styles of heists. Without spoiling exactly how this happens, you're told how to go about taking on such criminal ventures, and you can continue to do so throughout the game at your pleasure. Still, even after you've been tutorialised, pulling off one of these heists is no joke, and can easily turn chaotic.

This GTA 6 robbery sequence was CRAZY, I couldn't even think straight . pic.twitter.com/l65xSFRoSr.

Here's a little tip for those of you looking to pull off a heist yourself. You're told that safety deposit boxes can be rifled through for additional loot. However, when you actually make your way into a vault, these will be closed without much sign on which you can access. If you use the focus mode (by pushing in both L3 and R3), it will highlight boxes which you can shoot open. This, of course, may garner unwanted attention, so whether or not you think it's worth doing is part of the risk/reward dilemma you'll have to reckon with. As is the case with so much stuff in GTA 6 including, but not limited to, car-jacking.

Sources indicate that if you're looking to get your life of crime properly underway, you can read our GTA 6 robberies page for a breakdown on how it works. Alternatively, for a wider view of the game, our GTA 6 walkthrough is the way to go.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, ubisoft, they of the recently revealed generative AI-focused game studio Motherbrain, have denied they're forcing upcoming games being pitched by their developers to integrate use of genAI as a rule.
  • The report from Vertical Slice cited anonymous Ubisoft staff as having mentioned that the publishers' game pitching process now requires devs to either outline how they'll use generative AI to speed up production, or offer a specific justification as to why the tech isn't being used.
  • It has been revealed that ubisoft management reportedly revealed the change during a presentation to staff, with one source telling Vertical Slice that the tech giant are all in on generative AI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, ubisoft, they of the recently revealed generative AI-focused game studio Motherbrain, have denied they're forcing upcoming games being pitched by their developers to integrate use of genAI as a rule. The publishers' statement comes in the wake of a report claiming that Ubisoft devs with pitches that don't use genAI are required to explain in detail why they've decided it isn't suitable for the game being outlined.

The report from Vertical Slice cited anonymous Ubisoft staff as having mentioned that the publishers' game pitching process now requires devs to either outline how they'll use generative AI to speed up production, or offer a specific justification as to why the tech isn't being used.

It has been revealed that ubisoft management reportedly revealed the change during a presentation to staff, with one source telling Vertical Slice that the tech giant are all in on generative AI. They cited an "attitude shift" among Ubisoft management as having left workers feeling "cornered by generative AI all the time", but made clear Ubisoft haven't brought in a blanket mandate forcing devs to use genAI no matter what.

Industry observers note that ubisoft have emphasised the latter in a statement subsequently issued to Vertical Slice. "We encourage our teams to explore where AI can be useful and bring value to their work," the tech giant wrote. "This doesn’t mean that projects are required to use generative AI. Teams need to determine whether, and how, these technologies make sense for the game they want to make and the experience they want to create for players.".

In a recent development, ubisoft have been keen on experimenting with genAI in game development for a little while - something essentially set in stone by the establishing of Motherbrain as a proper division where the manufacturer can work on the likes of the "first playable generative AI experience" they were shouting about earlier this year. That move came in a year Ubisoft have spent vast swaths of laying off staff and closing studios, as part of a restructuring they kicked off with a barrage of cancellations in January.

Industry observers note that most recently, those cuts hit 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on a list of other affected subsidiaries that I'm very much getting tired of wheeling out whenever Ubisoft inevitably insist on adding to it.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that when it was confirmed that Robert Pattinson had been cast as James Bond, Twilight fans everywhere did a little cheer.
  • According to recent reports, first off, in case you missed it, James Bond is brought up around 58 minutes into 2008’s Twilight.
  • Twilight literally predicted Robert Pattinson being James Bond btw https://t.co/eMfeaVhbhuNovember 16, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when it was confirmed that Robert Pattinson had been cast as James Bond, Twilight fans everywhere did a little cheer. Especially if you were Team Edward! What a good long-term investment that’s turned out to be! However, the most popular Twilight-related reaction to Pattinson being 007 stems from the fact that the iconic spy was brought up in the vampire movie. As it turns out, there’s a whole new layer to that scene we didn’t know about.

According to recent reports, first off, in case you missed it, James Bond is brought up around 58 minutes into 2008’s Twilight. Just seconds before Edward Cullen and Bella Swan make their grand entrance as a couple for the first time at school, one of their classmates, Eric, hands out flyers for the upcoming prom, which is a Monte Carlo theme. Check out the scene below:.

Twilight literally predicted Robert Pattinson being James Bond btw https://t.co/eMfeaVhbhuNovember 16, 2026.

In a recent development, isn’t that wild? James Bond is literally noted in Twilight right before the current James Bond appears. However, there’s more to it. The movie’s director, Catherine Hardwicke, revealed something new about the scene while talking about the casting on The Kyle Buchanan Show. In her words:.

It has been revealed that I noted, ‘Let’s put the sunglasses on that day,’ and he got out of the car and he looked so suave that he inspired the line Bond, James Bond… Justin kind of ad-libbed it. It’s kind of cool because we did think he looked like James Bond. So, I guess we were seeing the future.

Recent findings suggest that that happened 18 years before it became a reality. I guess it goes to show the role has been right for Robert Pattinson all along given those on the set of Twilight were thinking about it, too. Pattinson didn’t earn the role easily, either. All sorts of other eligible actors such as Nicholas Hoult, Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden reportedly auditioned for Denis Villeneuve’s film. Charlie Cox also recently remarked he was shot down for being “too old” even though he’s just three years older than Pattinson.

Hardwicke certainly had a hand in making Pattinson the major name he is. And, while talking about the actor, she recalled what stuck out about him when he auditioned for Twilight. In her words:.

He’s intense, and he’s interesting, and he’s got a lot of stuff going on in there, and he’s weird and he’s original. He doesn’t fit the mold and he’s not scared to think or say crazy shit, which is what I love about him.

Recent findings suggest that while it’s perhaps a bit surprising Amazon MGM Studios didn’t opt for an actor who was an unknown, Jeff Bezos has said that in the screen tests it was “so obvious” Pattinson was their Bond that they didn’t dare pick anyone else. We can’t wait to see what his Bond will be like, and given his career thus far, it sounds like it might be unexpected.

While we wait for Bond 26, you can get excited to see Robert Pattinson in Dune: Part 3 on December 18. Oh, and the whole Twilight saga is there for anyone with a Netflix subscription.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar Games is seemingly interested in expanding Red Dead Redemption beyond video games, after years of Hollywood knocking on its doors.
  • Industry observers note that the information comes from a newly introduced report in The Ankler, citing agents in the know.
  • Recent findings suggest that rockstar, however, is not interested in turning Grand Theft Auto into a movie or TV show, per the same report.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar Games is seemingly interested in expanding Red Dead Redemption beyond video games, after years of Hollywood knocking on its doors. According to a new report, the company is looking for someone to pick up the movie and TV rights for its open-world Westerner series.

Industry observers note that the information comes from a newly introduced report in The Ankler, citing agents in the know. According to the report, Rockstar wanted something in the range of $100m (£76m) as a minimum for the license to its Red Dead Redemption series of games. As the report pointed out, Amazon paid $250m (£191m) in 2017 for Lord of the Rings' TV show rights alone.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar, however, is not interested in turning Grand Theft Auto into a movie or TV show, per the same report. It's not clear why the company is willing to entertain the idea for one franchise and not the other, but the vastly larger popularity of GTA (compared to RDR, at least) could explain why.

It's worth noting that streamers like Netflix and Amazon have been on something of a hot streak recently with the success of demonstrates based on popular video games, such as Fallout. HBO managed to turn The Last of Us into a prestige series that can attract both fans of the game and casual TV viewers.

Indeed, many more video game-based shows are in the works, like Amazon's Tomb Raider series, its God of War adaptation, as well as FX's Far Cry anthology show. Even Call of Duty, a massive - though nowhere near as massive as GTA - franchise, is getting a live-action movie in 2028.

But none of those are as profitable or culturally-dominnant as Grand Theft Auto. GTA 6 just released, and immediately beat analyst expectations. The game made $3.79bn (£2.90bn) in revenue on day one off the back of 32.5m copies sold, making it the biggest launch of any entertainment product in history, so it's understandable why Rockstar is not too eager to turn it into a movie or TV show.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 hasn't even been out for a week yet, and someone has already done the math on how many buildings in the whole of Leonida you can actually walk into. For those of you who are curious: it's 1,563 buildings.

That is frankly ridiculous. I don't think I've ever been inside 1,563 different buildings in my entire life, although I am a creature of habit, so that could explain things. The player who shared these stats, Aileos, does note that there are 5,588 buildings in total, so the enterable buildings only account for a fraction of that, just over 25%.

It has been revealed that there are some who will look at this with a glass-half-empty perspective, and I get it. This world is so cool, it's easy to want more of it, but as another player points out, "This would've sent us into psychosis a few years back". Sometimes it's better to focus on what we have rather than what we don't have. After all, how many buildings will you realistically enter in your GTA 6 playthrough? Probably not 1,563.

Sources indicate that we've spent the past week here in the PC Gamer Slack channel marvelling at just how many random encounters you can stumble across in GTA 6. Some of us have found sentient NPCs. One of us was actually recognised by a convenience store clerk who then asked to get robbed, and I think we've all seen videos of the furry rescue mission.

But just because this world already has loads of awesome activities, it doesn't mean we aren't hoping for more. A massive casino and go-kart track have been spotted by players, both of which have huge "Coming Soon" signs draped outside of them.

It has been revealed that these buildings could be lying in wait for GTA 6 Online, or they could be added to singleplayer sometime in the future. Regardless, those are two more buildings that will potentially welcome players soon.

Unofficial GTA 6 PC port effort suffers setback as Rockstar seemingly takes down Project Leonida, one of the internet's biggest recompilation projects

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that A lot has happened in the last 24 hours in the community working to get Grand Theft Auto 6 running on PC.
  • After infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6, the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers.
  • Sources indicate that the largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A lot has happened in the last 24 hours in the community working to get Grand Theft Auto 6 running on PC. And now, Rockstar has dealt a major blow to their efforts.

After infamous leaker CyberLeek made good on their promise and released a full Xbox build of GTA 6, the build immediately spread online amongst modders and recompilers. Their goal? Get the game playable on PC as soon as possible.

Sources indicate that the largest hub of all that activity has been the Project Leonida Discord server, which had its own repository and a team of volunteer modders working - with help from Claude AI - to recompile GTA 6's leaked Xbox build to run on PC. Rockstar has allegedly taken down the server, causing the project's leaders to dismantle the entire operation.

Project Leonida's lead NotRexed posted on X to announce they're ending development, after fans noticed the Discord server has been removed, as has Project Leonida's GitHub repository.

"I quit guys. I'm sorry," NotRexed wrote. "I really want to make cool stuff but every single time shit happens that I can't control so I'm stepping away. Thank you everybody, especially in the discord that allowed me to have this opportunity.".

The modder, who claims to be a "15 year-old kid", later wrote in a follow-up X post that Rockstar is behind the server's takedown, though that's not the only reason for the project's end.

"Last post from me. I wanna clear things up," they wrote. "Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've remarked before, I'm a 15 year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.".

Recent findings suggest that before the Project Leonida server disappeared, footage emerged showing GTA 6 running on PC. The game is able to reach the initial setup screen, but rapidly goes into a black screen afterwards. As unimpressive as the result was, it was achieved within hours of the full Xbox build's leak.

In a recent development, incidentally, while Project Leonida was the biggest and most prominent of the various GTA 6 recompilation projects, the leaking of the full Xbox build has given rise to various other groups. PortWatch VI is a website dedicated to tracking their progress, and though the data is almost entirely self-reported, a few other teams appear to have made notable progress themselves, so this may not be the end of the story.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar has yet to comment publicly on the Xbox build's leak, and the tech giant has not confirmed GTA 6 for PC. However, a report suggested GTA 6 arrives on PC in the first quarter of 2027, earlier than everyone expected.

If you're among the millions already playing the game on consoles, Eurogamer's GTA 6 walkthrough contains a wealth of information covering all major mechanics, main missions, secrets, cheats and more besides.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's been an exciting addition to the Nintendo Classics GameCube app today, as people have discovered a small - but oft-requested - change in the software's Version 2.2.0.

According to recent reports, this latest option arrived fairly quietly as part of an update that otherwise introduced Wave Race: Blue Storm to the Nintendo Classics – GameCube lineup. That addition may have generated the most headlines, but it's this one little toggle that's getting many players exicted.

Why is this such a significant deal? Previously, the bordered image on the 4:3 aspect ratio games contained lots of little dots, and players complained that these were distracting at best, and casused discomfort on the eyes whilst playing at worst. Other players worried it would contribute to screen burn-in on older televsion sets. As part of the upcoming revision, you can simply border your games with plain black - a tiny revision, but one that you can already see online communities celebrating. The player icon (another UI element that attracts derision) is still present, however, but as one comment summarises: "it's a step in the right direction".

In a recent development, "Oh my gawd, I've been wanting this! I hate the checkered on the side, it clashed with every game I tried," says one social media user." Players have been complaining about these borders and UI elements since Nintendo Classics was introduced on the Nintendo Switch back on 18th September, 2018. So it's taken a good eight years for Nintendo to - finally - implement a change.

In order to change the border yourself, you need to head to the game library selection screen on the Nintendo Classics app, navigate to the game settings, and locate the option to toggle this border graphic in the "Extra Elements Display" tab. Hit the button and - bang - you're done. At the time of writing, this option only appears on the GameCue app, and only on Switch 2, but people on social media are already asking Nintendo to enable it across the original Switch and other apps in the library, too.

Industry observers note that not everyone is happy with the 'slowly, slowly' approach Nintendo is taking towards implementing these changes, though. "Why can't we expect the full step with no graphic at all?" asks one irritated poster on Reddit. "Why do you have to deal with these half assed implementations for a paid deluxe subscription service?".

"Oh well, probably gotta wait another 10 years for the next improvement" states another. Another slightly more constructive user outlines what helpful additons might look like, noting that adding a "blurred zoomed in image of the game to fill out the background, or just extending the colors outward into the border, or maybe something fun like a CRT TV-looking border like the NES and SNES Classic had" would go a long way to make the retro experience better on the consoles.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Atari Homebrew Awards, an annual celebration of upcoming games developed for old systems by the people who love them both, has been cancelled after eight years of operation—and yes, it's because of AI.

Sources indicate that "As you may know, the landscape of retro game development changed dramatically this year with the massively increased capabilities of LLMs. More and more games have incorporated AI elements into their development chain and now have the capability to create full games without writing a single line of code," Atari Homebrew Awards host James, aka ZeroPage Homebrew, wrote on the Atari Age forums.

"Keeping up with the large number of AI-assisted game development had become increasingly difficult as this year wore on, with some developers even releasing multiple games a week with the aid of AI. This flood of newly introduced AI games forced me to re-evaluate the way games were qualified and judged for the upcoming AHAs.

It has been revealed that "The Atari Homebrew Awards were now challenged to make sure the work of human developers were still honoured amongst the upcoming fully computer-coded games. I was not at all interested in giving awards to the output of large language models, only to humans who coded their own games, but I rapidly discovered that this was going to be more difficult than I thought.".

James remarked he discovered last week that "a large majority" of developers were using AI in some capacity to make their games, from testing to wholesale game creation, "without one typed line of code.".

That left two options: Disallow any and all AI usage in the Atari Homebrew Awards competition, which James said would disqualify a large number of "extremely talented coders" who used AI in some very minor way, or let it slide and either choose an arbitrary dividing line between what is and isn't allowed or allow everything, including fully vibe-coded games.

Sources indicate that james stated he wasn't interested in that, which meant he needed to settle on how much AI usage would be allowable—and also how to determine if AI was used at all, since some developers are better at disclosure than others. That, naturally, led to the worry that developers could be subject to "false positives and possible witch hunts," something that's already a problem in mainstream game development.

This is an extremely upsetting conclusion for this event because honouring all the hard work the community put into these games is always a highlight of my year.

Recent findings suggest that ultimately, James decided there was no practical way forward, although he did leave open the possibility of a return someday. "This is an extremely upsetting conclusion for this event because honouring all the hard work the community put into these games is always a highlight of my year," he wrote. "I know many others feel the same way and I hope to be able to continue this tradition in the coming years as things settle into a newly introduced normal.".

As we noted in July, debates over "acceptable" levels of AI use are cropping up all over the open source development scene: Some are drawing hard lines against it for principled and/or practical reasons, yet its popularity is growing explosively because, frankly, you don't need to know what you're doing in order to do it—as long as you're not too concerned with doing it well.

The Atari Homebrew Awards isn't the first such event to fall victim to the AI flood. Earlier in November, the Australian STEM Videogame Challenge, a "free national videogame development competition for students," confirmed that the 2026 event will be its last because "the rapid and complex rise of generative AI in game development [made] it harder to judge what students made themselves," and thus undercut the whole purpose of the program: Encouraging kids to learn how to code.
